1.en: Leina's servant, who can transform into three forms: robot, jet helicopter and supercar. Technically a member of the Jet tribe. Because Triple Jim can carry members of the Cronos tribe, Jim is a great help when traveling, but is poor at fighting because of a gentle nature. That said, Jim understands how martial artists feel, and often put Jim's own body on the line for Leina's sake. Always humble and polite in speech, Jim shouts "It is above you, if you please!" even when warning someone that something is falling from above. In episode 24, Jim performed a catchphrase imitating Rom's. Jim also seems to be able to use Tenku Chushin Ken, though only a little.
1.notes: Gender of Triple Jim is unknown in the glossary, so no gendered pronouns are used.
uncertain: Gender unknown: 'Jim' repeated instead of a pronoun.
The line shouted ('above, if you please') is a paraphrase of the polite 'ue de gozaimasu'.

2.name_jp: トリプル・ジム・スーパーカー
2.en: Triple Jim's supercar form. In the original story, Triple Jim usually carried Leina in this form when they traveled. Incidentally, Rom rode a machine called Flex.
uncertain: 'Flex' = Battle Flex on English Wikipedia (Rom's jeep).

3.name_jp: トリプル・ジム・ヘリ
3.en: Triple Jim's jet helicopter form. In an emergency, Triple Jim makes high-speed trips in this form.

5.name_jp: パワーライザー（レイナ）
5.en: Reinforced armor for the Cronos tribe, built by Wrestler Robo for Rom after Kenro was taken from him. According to Rom, it is "a magnificent design with absolutely no waste." The arms and legs are linked to the wearer's brain waves, so the wearer can move them at will, as if they were the wearer's own body. However, because it is controlled by brain waves, it has the weakness that it becomes uncontrollable if the wearer's anger is too intense, and the arms and legs stop moving entirely if the wearer freezes in fear. It can also dash at high speed using rollers and fly for short periods using thrusters, and Rom used this Power Riser to perform Tenku Chushin Ken techniques.
5.notes: The library text describes Rom's use of the Power Riser; the entry itself is the Leina variant.
uncertain: 'Wrestler Robo' is a literal translation of the kana (no English source).
Who took Kenro is not stated in this entry (Garudi in the series).

6.en: A warrior of the Jet tribe who, like Rom and Drill, trained under Kirai. He was taught Tenku Shin Ken by Kirai. As his name suggests, he can transform into a jet aircraft. Within Rom's party he is the cool, handsome type, who dashes in to rescue friends and beautiful women in their moment of crisis. He is also quite sharp, and often served as Rom's strategist. His only built-in weapon is the sword stored at his waist, from which he unleashes various secret techniques of Tenku Shin Ken. The Blazer Cannon is an additional weapon that appeared from the middle of the original story; it has the same name as Rod Drill's, but the cannon on Jet fires beams.

7.name_jp: ブルー・ジェット（変形）
7.en: Blue Jet's flight form. In exchange for losing the use of his sword, Vulcans and the Blazer Cannon become usable as built-in weapons. In the original story, he also sometimes traveled with Rom hanging from him. Incidentally, the shout of "Je-e-et!" when transforming into this form was first thought up by Blue Jet and became popular among the Jet tribe.

8.en: A fellow disciple of Rom and Jet. He is from the Battle tribe and transforms into a drill tank. Cheerful and bold, he excels at power-based fighting. He was something of a mood maker within the party, yet repeatedly saved his companions from danger with that drill. He is the type who sleeps a full 10 hours, and apparently once punched Jet in his sleep when Jet came to wake him. He has no built-in weapons, and since his trademark drill cannot be used in this form either, he fights with his fists alone, but he rarely shouts technique names; the only one confirmed is "Tenku Chushin Ken: Head-Hunting." The Blazer Cannon differs from Jet's in the shape of its muzzle, and is a missile launcher.
uncertain: 'Tenku Chushin Ken: Head-Hunting' is my translation of the technique name (no English source).
'Fellow disciple' for the kana 'brother disciple'.

9.en: Rod Drill's drill tank form. With drill charges and Vulcans, it has more armament than the humanoid form, and it can burrow underground. For some reason, Drill seems to be afraid of spiders and long, thin things (Cronos earthworms). In addition, Drill is used to handling explosives and is surprisingly an artist, making him a rather mysterious character.
uncertain: 'Drill charges' is the translation of the plain word 'drill assault' ([jp]); could also be 'charges with the drill'.

10.en: A medium-sized robot that Rom merges with. Its name is written with the characters for "sword" and "dragon." When the energy of light reaches its peak, Kenro crosses the dimensional wall and summons Kenryuu. By merging with Kenryuu, Rom is able to display tens of times his usual strength. Kenryuu often fights using Kenro, and, like Tenku Chushin Ken, makes frequent use of Tenku Shin Ken.

11.en: A giant robot that Rom merges into, from Kenryuu. Its name is written with the characters for "double" and "kung fu." The merge into Baikanfu is specifically called the Pile Formation. When Kenro, receiving Rom's will, turns to light in midair, the Pile Formation is completed, transcending time and dimensions. Baikanfu synchronizes with all the energy on the earth's surface and can produce power capable of changing even natural phenomena. It makes relatively frequent use of electric-type techniques such as Lightning Smash and Thunder Punch, but it has many other techniques as well, each carrying one-hit-kill destructive power. The shield used by Kenryuu can, like Kenro, also be used in the Baikanfu state.
uncertain: 'All the energy on the earth's surface' ([jp]) could also mean 'all the energy on the ground'.
'Pile Formation' is a translation of the katakana (no English source).

66.en: A mass-production Dragonar. A main weapon of the Earth Alliance Forces, built at the secret weapons factory in Chongqing by making use of the combat data of the D-Weapons. Equipped with an excellent auto-sensor, it has, on paper, the combined capabilities of three machines: Dragonar-1, Dragonar-2 and Dragonar-3. Although it was given what, when you think about it, is only natural for a mass-production machine (specs superior to the prototypes), for the sake of the story it ended up as nothing more than a mecha that exists to be beaten.
uncertain: 'Earth Alliance Forces' follows the game's wording ([jp]); the official Sunrise site says 'Earth Federation'.

70.en: A prototype Metal Armor developed as a close-combat unit with excellent mobility, called by the abbreviation "D-1." Metal Armor is the general term for the humanoid mobile weapons developed by the Giganos Empire, and it developed from lunar work robots called Metal Workers. As this suggests, the Dragonars were made in Giganos but were seized by the Earth Alliance, and the three units together are also called the "D-Weapons." For the Earth Alliance, which lacks Metal Armor development technology, the D-Weapons are trump-card machines for turning the tide. The main armament is a 75 mm hand rail gun and close-combat laser swords mounted on both hips; the two laser swords can be joined to make a twin sword. Both shoulders also carry grenades called shoulder bombs. By being fitted with Lifter-1, a flight unit for atmospheric flight, the D-1, which already boasted high combat power, gained mobility and was powered up further. Incidentally, the D-1's computer is nicknamed Clara.

71.name_jp: ドラグナー１型カスタム
71.en: A D-1 that underwent reinforcement modifications at the hands of Dr. Lang Plato. By incorporating know-how gained from developing the Dragoon and the Alliance's own technology, its mid-range combat and search-and-detection abilities have been improved, and its original close-combat ability has also been powered up. The two laser swords are mounted on the left hip, and a throw-in bomb is equipped on the right hip. Also, because a gravity field detection system was installed on the left shoulder, the shoulder bombs have been reduced to a single one on the right shoulder.
uncertain: 'Throw-in bomb' ([jp]) is a literal rendering of the kana; no English source.

72.en: A prototype Metal Armor developed for long-range support. Abbreviated "D-2." Its main armament is the 280 mm rail cannons on both shoulders, which alone have enough firepower to smash an enemy in one hit, and it also has a wealth of optional equipment such as twin Gatling cannons and rocket launchers, making it an extremely heavily armed machine. It does carry an assault knife for close combat, but it is poor at close-range fighting. The D-2's flight unit, Lifter-2, has a refueling system and can also refuel the other two machines. Incidentally, the D-2's computer is nicknamed Sonia.

73.name_jp: ドラグナー２型カスタム
73.en: A reinforced and modified D-2. Unlike the D-1 Custom, which raised overall performance, the modification focused on raising firepower, the D-2's greatest feature. The rail cannons on both shoulders have become a large 640 mm caliber, and the twin automatic cannons that were omitted when the Lifter is worn have been revived. In addition, twin heavy dual missiles have been newly added to the legs. Naturally, armor and generator output have also been increased.

74.en: A prototype Metal Armor developed for electronic warfare. With excellent reconnaissance, detection and intelligence-gathering abilities, it supports the combat operations of the D-1 and D-2 and disrupts the enemy. It can also hack enemy base computers and neutralize enemy holograms, so its field of activity is broad. However, since it is not a combat machine, its armor and armament are kept to a minimum, and various sensors and radars are embedded in their place. Lifter-3, the flight unit for the D-3, is likewise a lightweight type that emphasizes speed, and the D-3 has the highest speed of the three machines. Incidentally, the D-3's computer is nicknamed Maggie.

75.en: The D-3 shows no change in outward appearance, but its electronic warfare equipment has been updated in both software and hardware. Armor and thrust have also been improved, so it can be said that it has effectively become a custom model.

129.en: A defensive fighter owned by Daimobic. Its pilots are Kyoshiro Yuzuki and Nana Izumi, and its main mission is supporting Daimos. It has two Vulcans behind the cockpit and missiles under the main wings, and sometimes fired beams from the antenna-like part on its nose. Its combat power is surprisingly high, and it saved Daimos from danger many times. Of course, it can also operate in space. Also, perhaps because its pilot Kyoshiro is skilled, it showed considerable maneuverability and dodged enemy attacks over and over, and was almost never shot down. For that reason it gives a very sleek impression compared with Daimos, which is always covered in scars.

130.en: A super robot built through the cooperation of Dr. Ryuzaki and Dr. Izumi. It was originally a trailer for underground development that was converted into a combat robot, and uses Daimolite as its energy source. Daimolite is crystallized light born from a neutrino reaction; the light particles solidified under high gravity collide violently with one another and thereby keep emitting enormous energy. Also, Daimolite triggers a nuclear reaction and explodes massively at 4 degrees Celsius or above, and when fully released, it turns Daimos itself into a pure energy body. Because Daimos has a control system that traces the pilot's movements, it reproduces Kazuya's karate techniques without the slightest error, but conversely it has the weakness that when Daimos takes damage, the pilot takes damage too. Its weapons are mostly mid- and close-range ones such as the Five Shooter and the Triple Dragon Staff, making it a machine that emphasizes close combat. Also, the "Deadly Gale Correct Fist Thrust" was originally not a combination technique with Blizzard-type weapons but the name of the karate technique itself that delivers the finishing blow; likewise, following up from Blizzard-type weapons, it also used the "Deadly Gale Hand-Blade Thrust" and the "Deadly Daimos Chop."
uncertain: '4 degrees Celsius or above' is as written in the source (it looks odd but is the original figure).
Technique names are translated from the Japanese; see glossary weapons for the SRW wiki basis.

131.en: An all-purpose fighter owned by Mutropolis. It was used for many purposes, including not only combat but also reconnaissance, investigation and rescue operations. In the original story, it has a crew of three, and the upper part of the cockpit is a small aircraft, the Spit Fighter, which also serves as an escape device.
uncertain: 'Spit Fighter' ([jp]) is a literal rendering of the kana.

132.en: A mystical super robot built through the science of the ancient Mu Empire 12,000 years ago. Normally it is stored in a golden base-body state inside Divine Face Rock, and it starts moving when Akira climbs into it (fade-in). It uses the mysterious energy Mutron, and the Mutron metal used in its armor exhibits self-repair ability by returning to the base-body state. There are also many parts of its interior that remain unexplained, and in the latter half of the original story it showed its true power through a Mutron energy release device called the Star of Ra Mu. Its main finishing move is Godbird, in which it transforms into a bird form and charges at Mach 7. Raideen can be piloted only by Akira, who carries the blood of Ra Mu, emperor of the Mu Empire, and its control method is a unique one that is integrated with Akira's body movements.
uncertain: 'Divine Face Rock' ([jp]): ja Wikipedia writes [jp] (Human-Face Rock); kept the game's wording.

133.en: Raideen's bird-shaped flight form, mainly used when traveling long distances. It also takes this form when using the finishing move "Godbird," in which it sets its aim on an opponent's weak point and charges. There is much about its internal structure that is unknown, and from the middle of the story onward it comes to use a brutal technique called Head Cutter.

157.en: A powerful commander who once even took the No. 1 spot in the Gyandlar Commander ranking, in place of Devil Saturn 6. Ashura fires Nattoru bullets, which rob the target of bodily freedom, from the abdomen, and specializes in destroying the immobilized opponent in cruel ways. By nature Ashura is cruel and cunning, and once set a trap by turning Rom's party's surprise attack plan against them. Ashura drove Baikanfu into a corner, but was pierced through the chest by Thunder Cyclone and defeated.
157.notes: Library entry 157; the batch label was the placeholder 'none' (unit-table name Asura, kana Ashura).
uncertain: Gender of Asura unknown: no pronouns used.
'Nattoru bullet' is romanized from kana (no English source).

158.en: The boss of the space crime organization Gyandlar. Gyandlar's goal is to rule the entire universe and bring darkness and fear. It is also searching for Hyribead, an infinite energy said to grant eternal life. Gades is a villain who has wandered space for thousands of years piling up evil deeds, and trusts no one but himself. His sorcerous power is such that he can paralyze enemies in distant places. He attacked planet Cronos after Hyribead, but his ambition was thwarted by the Cronos tribe warriors, including Rom. He hates having rust form on his body to an extreme degree, and always kept with him a dedicated robot, Bibibi Mouse, to polish his body.
158.notes: Batch label was 'Gades' (kana [jp]) with series Machine Robo: correct.
uncertain: Gender male per ja Wikipedia/voice actors (glossary).
'Bibibi Mouse' romanized from kana.

159.en: A low-ranking Gyandlar Commander. When first introduced, Kyasumodon appeared as the main enemy and tried to set the Cronos tribe and the Battle tribe against each other, but after that appeared in large numbers as a grunt. Kyasumodon can transform into a flight form like a jet aircraft.
uncertain: Gender unknown: 'Casmodon' repeated.

160.en: One of the Gyandlar executives. Fond of underhanded schemes and plots, Grujios serves as a kind of strategist for Gyandlar. With tremendous sorcerous power, Grujios can revive the ghosts of Gyandlar Commanders and use them as servants. In truth, the real body is only a caterpillar-like face floating in the tank of the head. Grujios was defeated by Rom in the Battle of the Heavenly Demon Castle, but, just as promised in the "I shall return" warning, came back in spirit form. After becoming a spirit, Grujios gained a new ability to take over other people's bodies, and tormented Rom's party by posing as an ally.
uncertain: Gender unknown: no pronouns used.
'Battle of the Heavenly Demon Castle' is my translation of the event name.

161.en: A low-ranking Gyandlar Commander. Zarios is characterized by caterpillar-track legs, but had no especially notable role in the original story.

162.en: A female Gyandlar executive. In contrast to Grujios, so to speak, she often takes direct command at the front lines. Devil Saturn 6 are her direct subordinates. Wielding an electromagnetic whip, her speech and attitude fit being called "Big Sis," but she gets angry when called that. She is bold and cruel by nature, and tries to compete with Grujios at every turn. She also has a cute side in that she is actually afraid of earthquakes, and in the original story she almost got on good terms with Tough Trailer for a moment. After that, she set a trap for Tough Trailer by making that character hold the Medusa demon sword, a cursed blade that drives its holder mad, but after that scheme failed, she herself came to favor the Medusa demon sword. She can also breathe fire from her mouth and emit hypnotic light from her eyes.
uncertain: Tough Trailer's gender is not sourced, so no pronoun is used for that character.
'Big Sis' for the nickname Aneego (boss-lady / older-sister).

163.en: The combined form of Devil Saturn No. 1 through No. 6. Thanks to its viciousness and power it has held the No. 1 spot in the Gyandlar Commander ranking; it dropped in rank once, but soon came back. Its attacks are varied: not only fighting, but also flames from the mouth, claws launched on chains, beams from the eyes, and so on. It once even devised the Devil Foot Smash to counter God Hand Smash. It was often entrusted with Gyandlar's field operations, and was beaten up by Rom and the others time after time. It is a commander whose odd Kansai dialect makes it hard to hate, but in fact only Devil Saturn No. 1 actually uses the Kansai dialect, and the other five speak standard Japanese.
uncertain: 'Devil Saturn' vs. English Wikipedia 'Devil Satan'.
'God Hand Smash' is a translation of the kana (Rom/Baikanfu technique).

164.en: A low-ranking Gyandlar Commander. Its agility is its trait, but it seems not to have been depicted much in the original story.

165.en: An artificial weather satellite developed by Diondra. Fenomena No. 1 can not only generate thunderclouds artificially, but also make lightning strike a targeted location by laser guidance. The lightning has a terrifying power: a voltage of 10,000 volts and a temperature of over 30,000 degrees. Fenomena No. 2, developed later, was planned to disturb the geomagnetism of planet Cronos, destroy the ozone layer overhead, and make electromagnetic waves that drive Machine Robo mad rain down onto the surface, but through an unexpected accident it caused a pole shift on planet Cronos.
uncertain: Voltage figure is as written (10,000 V) although it looks low for lightning.

166.en: The fifth Angel confirmed. It has a regular octahedral exterior and attacks approaching enemies with a powerful charged particle cannon. To defeat this Angel, NERV used a hastily built modified positron cannon for EVAs (NERV spec) and carried out Operation Yashima, supplying it with electric power from all over Japan.
166.notes: Library entry 166; batch label was '[jp]' (name from the unit table: [jp]). Cross-series (Evangelion).

167.en: The thirteenth Angel confirmed. Hiding inside a cumulonimbus cloud, it came into contact with EVA-03, which was being transported to NERV's Second Experimental Site in Matsushiro, and completely took over Unit-03, which had just finished an activation test with Toji still aboard, and was designated an Angel. It went as far as defeating Unit-00 and Unit-02, but was destroyed by Unit-01, which had activated the Dummy System.

168.en: The fourteenth Angel confirmed. It invaded the Geofront from Tokyo-3 and, with overwhelming attack power beyond that of any previous Angel, defeated Unit-02 and Unit-00. In the end it fought the berserk Unit-01 and was devoured.

169.en: The Fifth Child dispatched by SEELE. His background, like Rei Ayanami's, is completely unknown. He has the amazing ability to change his synchronization rate at will, which astonished the NERV staff. He actively approached Shinji, and Shinji, too, opened his heart to Kaworu's straightforwardness and kindness. However, Kaworu was the seventeenth Angel, Tabris, sent in by SEELE, and he entered Terminal Dogma with the unmanned Unit-02 under his control. Then, of his own wish, he was crushed by Unit-01, in which Shinji rode. It is a well-known story that in the Japanese title of original episode 24, in which he appears, "The Final Messenger," joining the character for "shi" and the character for "sha" in the word "messenger" makes the surname of Kaworu: "Nagisa." See the entry "Kaworu Nagisa" in the character encyclopedia.
169.notes: Library entry 169; cross-series (Evangelion). The text is really about Kaworu Nagisa.
uncertain: The episode-24 wordplay is explained in prose; the Japanese characters cannot be shown in ASCII. Episode title rendered 'The Final Messenger' (official Netflix title).

170.en: The EVA series that SEELE, the secret organization that manages the Human Instrumentality Project, sent into NERV Headquarters to stop Gendo, who was advancing the plan outside its schedule. There are nine in total. Unlike the earlier series, the units' specifications include flight capability and S2 Engines as standard equipment. Dummy Plugs are used for activation and operation, and it seems that Kaworu Nagisa's data is in them.

171.en: The emperor of the Machine Empire Gulfer, which plots the extermination of humanity. Originally the ecosystem management computer of the planet Alktos, the Emperor suddenly ran out of control, and tried to eliminate humanity, which destroys ecosystems, and become the king who manages the universe itself. The main body consists of seven programs and has a form resembling a seven-headed dragon. The Gulfer Emperor and Zero function as mutual backup systems, and unless they are defeated at the same time they will revive. The Emperor is also protected by seven protections and can be defeated only by a simultaneous attack by seven Data Weapons.
uncertain: 'Alktos' per English Wikipedia ('Arcturus' is a possible alternate romanization of the kana).

172.en: A common soldier of the Machine Empire Gulfer. By taking in other machines it evolves into a Gulfer Machine Beast. A non-humanoid flying type (Type B) has also been confirmed.
172.notes: Library entry 172; cross-series (Dendoh). English Wikipedia name: 'Galfa Sotai'.

173.en: One of the Machine Professionals that infiltrated Earth hidden in meteorites; this one emerged from a meteorite that fell near Mikazuki Island. Machine Professionals are higher beings than Machine Beasts and possess advanced intelligence. It is good at high-speed aerial combat and can also transform into a flight form. The Photon Rifle is a versatile weapon that can also transform into a Photon Scythe.
uncertain: 'Machine Professional' for [jp] follows English Wikipedia ('Professional Machines').

174.en: One of the Machine Professionals that infiltrated Earth hidden in meteorites; this one emerged from a meteorite that fell in a wasteland on the Oceania continent. Its weapons are a photon laser fired from its forehead and electric shocks released from the wings on its back. It was the Machine Professional that dodged the Final Attack and remained to the end.
uncertain: Entries 173-175 and 181-182 are assigned to Virus/Error/Bug/Legacy/Lock by the unit-table offset; the English Wikipedia power lists do not match the library text exactly, so the Error/Bug assignment of 174/175 is the least certain.

175.en: One of the Machine Professionals that infiltrated Earth hidden in meteorites; this one emerged from a meteorite that fell in the Amazon jungle on the South American continent. It is good at tricky attacks with its freely extendable arms.

176.en: A Machine Beast born by taking in Earth's attack satellites. It was used in Gulfer's first descent operation, and eighteen in total have been confirmed. As they gathered to respond to Dendoh's activation, they were all wiped out together by the Flash Lightning Blade Strike.
uncertain: 'Flash Lightning Blade Strike' ([jp]) translated literally; no English source.

177.en: A Machine Beast born by taking in a Defense Force fighter plane. Since it is based on a fighter plane, it has a variety of attacks such as missiles and machine guns.

178.name_jp: 機将ギガアブゾルート
178.en: One of the three officers of Spiral Castle. According to Ginga, "the third pompous guy." Its body is made of liquid metal, and it changes shape to dodge enemy attacks or entangle opponents. It also moves quickly and is good at surprise attacks, seeping into walls.
uncertain: Assignment of Absolute/Witter/Gourmet to 178/179/180 follows the unit-table order and matches the English Wikipedia power descriptions.

179.en: One of the three officers of Spiral Castle. According to Ginga, "a pompous kendama." It generates strong electromagnetic waves from its main body and has the ability to disable all electronic devices. Also, unless its head, the center, is destroyed, its body regenerates any number of times.
uncertain: 'Kendama' (cup-and-ball toy) kept as is.

180.en: One of the three officers of Spiral Castle. According to Ginga, "the pompous one, number two." It deploys an electromagnetic interference field around itself and has the ability to hinder the materialization of Data Weapons. It emits electric shocks from its arms and fires a beam cannon from its mouth. It is also quite a power fighter.

181.en: A Machine Professional that Subaru rides. Originally, like other Machine Professionals and Machine Beasts, it had thinking ability, but it has been modified so that a human can pilot it.
181.notes: Library entry 181; cross-series (Dendoh). The English spelling 'Legacy' is a guess from the kana (not on Wikipedia).

182.en: One of the Machine Professionals that infiltrated Earth hidden in meteorites; this one emerged from a meteorite that fell in the Sahara Desert on the African continent. It has the ability to make its whole body white-hot and explode everything around it.

183.en: A close aide of the Gulfer Emperor, and the supreme officer of Gulfer, who commands at the front lines in the Emperor's place. Excels at hand-to-hand combat and is good at staff fighting with an extendable ruyi staff. Also has the fearsome special ability to revive immediately even if destroyed. Often travels, or makes combined attacks, riding on the back of the heavy machine beast Vector, which has interstellar navigation ability.

184.en: Zero's strongest form, combined with the heavy machine beast Vector. Armed with a huge lancer and photon blasters fired from both shoulders, it is greatly powered up in both combat power and mobility. Incidentally, heavy machine beast is the general term for Machine Beasts that were promoted because they achieved results when Gulfer invaded other planets before attacking Earth, and having gained that much experience, they are individuals stronger than ordinary Machine Beasts.

185.en: A black Gear that forms a pair with Dendoh. It is also called Knight Ogre. Its basic abilities are the same as Dendoh's, but it has been modified to be single-seat. It is piloted by Altair, captain of the Gulfer Emperor's guard, and like Dendoh it has the ability to file-save Data Weapons.
185.notes: Library entry 185; cross-series (Dendoh). English Wikipedia: 'Knight Gear Oger'.
uncertain: 'Ouga' vs. Wikipedia 'Oger/Ogre'.

186.name_jp: 凰牙・バイパーウィップ
186.en: An Ogre fitted with Viper Whip. Viper Whip seeks "confidence," so Altair became its owner.

187.en: An Ogre fitted with Bull Horn. The "wisdom" that Bull Horn seeks was also greater in Altair.

188.en: A Machine Beast adjusted for capturing Data Weapons. Because of that purpose its combat ability is low, and it carries out operations in combination with other Machine Beasts.

189.en: The Gulfer Emperor's pet. It is not a mechanical life form, but a space creature that eats machines. For that reason, it is sometimes used to punish subordinates who failed. The Lagowe virus, a computer virus that is a deadly poison to machines, is implanted in the fangs hidden in Lagowe's huge jaws.

190.en: The master of Spiral Castle, sent to conquer Earth, called "Oyakata-sama" (the Lord). Three Machine Generals serve under it, and it is the apex of the pyramid that includes the Machine Beasts below them. A Spiral Castle is a unit of the Gulfer army, and countless Spiral Castles exist throughout the universe.
uncertain: 'Oyakata-sama' kept in romanization with a gloss.

191.en: A super-large battleship of the Jovian Federation. Over ten times the size of the Nadesico, it is closer to a fortress than a battleship. In the Lizard War, Commander-in-Chief Haruki Kusakabe boarded it, and it was operated as the flagship of the Yujin Corps of the Jovian Federation Forces.
uncertain: 'Yujin Corps' and 'Jovian Federation Forces' translated from the kana wording.

192.en: An unmanned combat weapon of the Jovian Federation. It is classified as an insect-type fighter in the Jovian Federation, but on Earth it is mainly called by the name of the creature whose shape it resembles. These unmanned combat weapons are produced at the phase transition engine plants discovered in the Jupiter region, and since they are products of an ancient civilization, overtechnology such as small anti-gravity propulsion devices is used.

193.en: An unmanned combat weapon of the Jovian Federation. Joro is a spider-type robot named for its resemblance to the Joro spider. The abdominal unit can be swapped for self-destruct explosives and other loads depending on the mission.

194.en: An unmanned combat weapon of the Jovian Federation. It is an upper-grade model of Batta, the most popular unmanned combat weapon. A field generator is attached, giving it excellent defense. Compared with Batta, machine guns have been removed in terms of armament, but it makes up for this with ramming attacks that take advantage of its high defense.

195.en: A manned humanoid combat weapon of the Jovian Federation. It is a weapon-reinforced version of Tetsujin, which was modeled on Gekiganger from Gekiganger 3, the sacred text of the Jovian Federation. The Jin series can make solo boson jumps without going through a Chulip, but the jump distance is limited to short range. Even so, that was sufficient for the purpose of breaking through the enemy front line and delivering a powerful blow to the core.

196.en: A manned humanoid combat weapon of the Jovian Federation. It is a weapon-reinforced version of Majin, which was modeled on Umiganger from Gekiganger 3, the sacred text of the Jovian Federation. Because the Jin series carry phase transition reactors, they are large machines exceeding 30 m, and the Dai class, the weapon-reinforced version, is larger still.
uncertain: 'Umiganger' and 'Rikuganger' are romanized from kana (no English source).

197.en: A manned humanoid combat weapon of the Jovian Federation. It is a machine modeled on Rikuganger from Gekiganger 3, the sacred text of the Jovian Federation. A late-model Jin, it was shaped with anti-field combat in mind so that close-combat ability does not decline after the Gekigan Punch is fired. Naturally, a weapon-reinforced Daidenjin was also planned, but the war ended before roll-out.

198.en: An unmanned destroyer of the Jovian Federation. Like other unmanned machines, it is also produced at the plants. Because it is mass-produced, it has the simplest block structure among the Jovian Federation's warships, and several variations can be made just by swapping the combat block and the power block.

199.en: A mobile weapon of the Martian Successors. Pronounced "Shishiki." Miniaturization was achieved by making the boson jump system an external unit. The Martian Successors' machines are developed, based on Kusakabe's philosophy, on the premise of assault tactics using boson jumps. Shishiki's boson jump is limited to a single use, and it excels at surprise attack and charge tactics that take advantage of that ability.

200.en: A machine of Hokushin's Six. Pronounced "Muzura." An airframe that omits the legs and emphasizes mobility, and it is also capable of a single-use boson jump through an external unit. It excels at "Kugutsu-mai" (Puppet Dance), an irregular mobile attack that uses rotating turret nozzles. Like Yatenko, it also has a field generator around the cockpit.
200.notes: Library entry 200; cross-series (Nadesico movie). The batch label was Iron Sand.
uncertain: 'Hokushin's Six' is a translation of [jp] (no English source).

201.en: A mobile weapon that Hokushin rides. Pronounced "Yatenko." It is a compact developed version of the Jin series that the Jovian Federation operated during the Lizard War, and although there is a limit on the number of times, it can make multiple mid-range boson jumps. Since it can move to the battlefield by boson jump, it uses fuel-type thrusters and excels at the irregular movement called "Kugutsu-mai" (Puppet Dance). It is also equipped with three small distortion field generators around the cockpit, making it a machine with high survivability.
201.notes: Library entry 201; cross-series (Nadesico movie). The batch label was Asura.

202.en: The prototype of a giant Metal Armor developed at the Giganos secret weapons factory. A walking ammunition depot with a 12-barrel chest machine cannon, a 100-tube missile pod, a quad Vulcan cannon, large cruise missiles and more built in. It carries a control system that allows operation by thought, enabling high mobility far beyond normal reaction speed. However, this system was unfinished and placed a heavy burden on the pilot, so it could not be used for long periods. In addition, the installed sensors had a serious flaw: they could not distinguish overlapping targets.
202.notes: Library entry 202; batch label was Gades. Unit-table name Gilgazamune.

203.en: Dorchenov's personal Gilgazamune. It is equipped with a long sword instead of an Azure Dragon sword. Unfortunately, the sensor flaw has not been fixed.
203.notes: Library entry 203; batch label was Casmodon. Variant of Gilgazamune.

204.en: A mass-production Gilgazamune. The huge close-combat HB saber fitted at the request of Colonel Gon Jem seems to have been officially adopted.
204.notes: Library entry 204; batch label was Grujios. Variant of Gilgazamune.

205.en: A prototype Metal Armor of the Giganos forces. A high-performance machine that Gon Jem used as his personal unit, but it seems it never reached mass production. The grenades at the waist and the Azure Dragon sword on the back seem to reflect Gon Jem's tastes. Its attack power was nonetheless high, and the Azure Dragon sword, coated with a special alloy, combined with Gon Jem's skill, was sharp enough to cut through even the D-1's shield. The cobra painted on the shoulder is the emblem of the Gon Jem Squad.
205.notes: Library entry 205; batch label was Zarios. Unit-table name Geizam ([jp]).

206.en: A machine made by fitting a MAFFU flight unit to the Gewai, the main mass-production Metal Armor of the Giganos forces. Its weapons are a 50 mm hand rail gun and a 30 mm machine cannon built into the camera-eye section. Because development of the MAFFU unit was rushed, its flight ability is somewhat inferior to the others.
206.notes: Library entry 206; batch label was Diondra.

207.en: A machine made by fitting a MAFFU flight unit to the Gelf, a high-performance Metal Armor deployed only in small numbers to the Practice Squad and the Imperial Guard Armored Division. The Gelfs that the Practice Squad ride are painted in special colors. It can be called a simplified Falguen, and has Simole Type-A passive armor and a radar more sensitive than a maiden's skin.
207.notes: Library entry 207; batch label was Devil Saturn 6.
uncertain: 'Imperial Guard Armored Division' vs. 'Armored Corps' used elsewhere (the library writes both [jp]/[jp]).

208.en: A bike-type Metal Armor. It can split into upper and lower parts and recombine, with the upper turret part called Dolla and the lower bike part called Ganzer. Dolla can transform into a semi-humanoid form and fly, and by swapping the lower part for Gelfer, it becomes Geldolla, a marine Metal Armor. It is used for parachute drop operations and the like.
208.notes: Library entry 208; batch label was Falgos. Unit-table name Stark Gandolla.
uncertain: 'Ganzer', 'Gelfer', 'Geldolla' are romanized from kana (no English source).

209.en: A Gewai customized exclusively for Captain Gol. It has not only been reinforced with a 450 mm rail cannon and hand grenades, but its output has also been greatly increased, making it a machine worthy of the brawny Captain Gol. The cockpit modifications must have been a lot of work.
209.notes: Library entry 209; batch label was Phenomena. Unit-table name Stark Gewei.
uncertain: The last sentence is the author's own conjecture in the Japanese; kept as a comment.

246.en: The giant battleship that King Vega boards. It was used when escaping the explosion of planet Vega, and flew to the Skull Moon base using the space transposition device Transportion. It fires powerful beams from the protrusions at the front of the hull, and can produce smoke to hide itself and a powerful barrier from the many holes on the side of the hull. In the end it is destroyed by the concentrated attack of the Grendizer team.
246.notes: Library entry 246; batch label was Gilgazamune. Cross-series (Grendizer).
uncertain: 'Transportion' is romanized from kana.

247.en: The first Vega Beast, stronger than the Saucer Beasts. Vega Beasts are wild animals turned into cyborgs, and have greater combat power than Saucer Beasts. In addition to power strong enough to tear off Grendizer's left arm, it has an excellent sense of smell, and can remember the scent of an opponent it has fought once and hunt that opponent down no matter where. Because its origin is a gorilla, it has a tendency to be afraid of fire. Also, as is the convention for an enlarged gorilla, it took Hikaru hostage and climbed to the top of a skyscraper and roared. It is the Vega Beast with the most memorable name.
247.notes: Library entry 247; batch label was Gilgazamune. Cross-series (Grendizer).

248.en: The strongest and last Vega Beast, which Lady Gandal boarded. A large amount of Vegatron energy was injected into it, and it has tremendous power and a sturdy body. It breathes high-temperature flames from its mouth, and the beams fired from the two protrusions on its chest not only damage the machine but also temporarily take away the opponent's sight.
248.notes: Library entry 248; batch label was Gilgazamune. Cross-series (Grendizer).

249.en: A Vega Beast piloted by Imperial Guard captain Morus. It originally had flesh, but on the last day of planet Vega, because Vega exploded when the transfer machine was activated, it was transferred by mistake to the very edge of the solar system, and on its way to Skull Moon it was reduced to bones by meteorites and cosmic rays. It fires powerful beams from its eyes and pierces enemies with the drill in its chest.
249.notes: Library entry 249; batch label was Geizam. Cross-series (Grendizer).

250.en: A Vega Beast equipped with a freezing ray, developed by the genius girl Kirika. It fires the freezing ray from its pupils and from the gem on its chest, and together with the blade on its right hand it gave Grendizer a hard time. The freezing ray was originally meant to cool the temperature of young planets, but was converted into a weapon by King Vega's order.
250.notes: Library entry 250; batch label was Gewei Maffu. Cross-series (Grendizer).

251.en: A giant saucer battleship that launches from the Skull Moon base on the Moon. Normally it is hung from the symbol tower of Skull Moon. Under the command of Captain Blacky, it served as a combat mothership carrying Saucer Beasts and Mini Fours. It has powerful beam cannons and sturdy armor.
251.notes: Library entry 251; batch label was Gelf Maffu. Cross-series (Grendizer).
uncertain: 'Mother Barn' vs. 'Mother Burn' (kana [jp]).

252.en: A medium-sized space saucer of the Vegan Empire forces. It is about twice the size of the Minifo, and its weapons are a Vegatron beam cannon and two missiles. Like the Minifo, it excels at group combat, but it was not much of a threat to Grendizer.
252.notes: Library entry 252; batch label was Stark Gandolla. Cross-series (Grendizer).
uncertain: 'Vega Star Union Forces' translated from the kana wording.

253.en: A small space saucer of the Vegan Empire forces. They appear in groups and attack in formation. Their weapons are Vegatron beam cannons and missiles. Besides combat, they are also used for reconnaissance and transport. They were a sufficient threat to the TFO, but because they were weak against Grendizer, most were destroyed in one hit. There are two kinds, for attack and for work, which differ in color.
253.notes: Library entry 253; batch label was Stark Gewei. Cross-series (Grendizer).

254.en: A Saucer Beast that sortied to support the Great Mazinger operated by Barendos. It attacks with disc-shaped arms with protrusions on the outside and three sharp legs. It is destroyed by the Atomic Punch of the Great Mazinger that Koji boarded.
254.notes: Library entry 254; batch label was Stark Deins. Cross-series (Grendizer vs. Great Mazinger).

255.en: A Saucer Beast that was inside the spherical giant beam cannon of the Barendos battleship. It is made of charged energy in the air, so no solid-projectile weapons work on it at all. It is broken apart by the Anti-Gravity Storm and Breast Burn, but it rammed Grendizer with the three spheres inside its body. Although it calls itself a Saucer Beast, it cannot transform into a saucer.
255.notes: Library entry 255; batch label was Stark Dautzen. Cross-series (Grendizer vs. Great Mazinger).

256.en: A Saucer Beast that Barendos deployed to capture the TFO. It extends its hook-claw-shaped hands to catch its opponent. It strangles Grendizer, which is fighting the Great Mazinger, from behind, but is destroyed by the Anti-Gravity Storm.
256.notes: Library entry 256; batch label was Deins Maffu. Cross-series (Grendizer vs. Great Mazinger).

257.en: A space monster that can be called both mechanical and biological, released into Japan by aliens plotting to conquer the Earth. It has a hard outer shell, a lizard-like face and an insect-type body, and spits out a dissolving liquid from its mouth. It grows by eating iron, and it ate the arm of the Great Mazinger.
257.notes: Library entry 257; batch label was Dreu. Cross-series (Mazinger movies).

258.en: Gilgilgan's second form. It has the appearance of a humanoid upper body growing out of the back of the first form. It has become able to shoot rays from the lizard eyes of the lower body.
258.notes: Library entry 258; batch label was Dragonar-1 Custom. Cross-series (Mazinger movies).

259.en: Gilgilgan's final form. It ate the aliens' saucer filled with cosmic energy, grew huge and became humanoid. It has wings and can fly. Its weapons are a sickle-like weapon on its waist and rays from its fingertips. It shows overwhelming strength, but its weak point is figured out to be the base of the sickle, and it is destroyed by a joint operation of the Great Mazinger and Getter Robo.
259.notes: Library entry 259; batch label was Falguen Maffu. Cross-series (Mazinger movies).

260.en: A weapon that looks like a space creature, released by mysterious aliens plotting to invade the Earth. It entangled Getter Robo with the tentacles growing all over its body and tried to slam it into the ground. It also fires strange rays from its eyes. It exploded from the suicide charge of Bear Go. It drove Musashi to his death.
260.notes: Library entry 260; batch label was Yakt Gelf Maffu. Cross-series (Mazinger movies).
uncertain: Name 'Gurangen' romanized from the kana; unverified.
'Musashi' = Musashi Tomoe (male) per Wikipedia; 'his death' follows from that.

261.en: A combat weapon of mysterious aliens. It is an assembly of fighter planes, tanks, the main guns of battleships and the like, and can fire from all over its body. It has the special ability to return to its original form again, if the individual parts are undamaged, even after being broken into pieces.
261.notes: Library entry 261; batch label was Levi Gelf Maffu. Cross-series (Mazinger movies).
uncertain: Name 'Bong' romanized from the kana; unverified.

262.en: The final combat weapon of mysterious aliens. Light wraps its whole body, and it absorbs beam and other light-ray energy and grows huge. Solid-projectile weapons, too, are deflected by the light. In addition to firing arrows of light that destroy the opponent from the inside, it has sharp claws and missiles from its chest. After the light was stripped away by the Great Typhoon and its mechanical body was exposed, it was destroyed by the Great Booster.
262.notes: Library entry 262; batch label was Dolla. Cross-series (Mazinger movies).
uncertain: Name 'Pikudoron' romanized from the kana; unverified.

263.en: A creature that had been lurking in the sea in ancient times, which revived and grew huge because humans spilled oil into the sea. For that reason it loves oil and attacks tankers. It can fly, and the dragon's-neck-shaped tentacles regenerate instantly even if cut, and can also be rotated to create strong winds. Also, its flexible body is immune to missile attacks.
263.notes: Library entry 263; batch label was Dautzen. Cross-series (Mazinger movies).

19.en: A boar-type data weapon that symbolizes "Creation." It has an impulsive, clumsy personality, and also serves as the leader of the data weapons. It rarely materialized to fight, but it was used frequently as a weapon. Its attribute is "Light."
uncertain: "it" used for the data weapon (no gender established)

20.en: A Cell Fighter fitted with a booster for use in space. The number of Hyper Dendoh Batteries it carries is greatly increased to 18, and its combat ability is also improved by the addition of a large beam cannon and missile pods, making it a heavy fighter for space combat.

22.en: A support mecha for Dendoh, developed in GEAR Britain. During battle, it swaps Dendoh's Hyper Dendoh Batteries from the air. It carries 4 batteries, which allows two battery changes. With the arrival of the Cell Fighter, Dendoh's ability to keep fighting improved dramatically, and the range of possible operational formations also widened.
uncertain: [jp] rendered "range of possible operational formations"

23.name_jp: セルブースターバルハラ
23.en: A second-unit Cell Fighter fitted with a space booster that emphasizes combat power. It carries 12 Hyper Dendoh Batteries and is equipped with a large long-range beam cannon and space mines. Because it was developed as Vega's dedicated machine, there is a hangar for the Valkyrie on the underside of the fuselage.

25.en: A dragon-type data weapon that symbolizes "Compassion." It has a calm, hard-to-please personality, is learned, and tends to love solitude. It often materialized to fight. Its attribute is "Flame."
uncertain: [jp] rendered "Compassion" (could also be "Benevolence")

26.en: The other Gear that stands as a pair with Dendoh. This is its state with the visor raised, revealing its true face. The technology used to convert Ogre into a one-person machine could also be applied to Dendoh, so for a time Dendoh was operated by a single pilot.

28.name_jp: 凰牙・ドラゴンフレア

29.name_jp: 凰牙・バイパーウィップ

30.name_jp: 凰牙・フェニックスエール
30.en: Ogre equipped with Phoenix Alae. Naturally, it also gains unlimited energy through Infinite Layer. When made into a weapon, Phoenix Alae takes the same names as Altair's beloved swords and becomes two swords, Kumogami and Minatsuchi.

31.name_jp: 凰牙・ユニコーンドリル

32.en: Ogre equipped with Kiba. When Ogre uses it, it becomes Kiba Breaker. Its Final Attack is a great sword of light that cuts the enemy in two.

33.en: A cobra-type data weapon that symbolizes "Confidence." It is delicate and shrewd, the type whose true thoughts cannot be read. It is the best schemer among the data weapons. Data weapons also have the role of unlocking the sealed abilities of the Gears, and it is said that something will happen when all six data weapons are gathered. Its attribute is "Lightning."

34.en: Dendoh equipped with a number of weapons that Dr. Inoue secretly built in case the data weapons became unusable. Many of the weapons use physical rounds or energy packs, so battery consumption can be kept down. They are basically disposable, and once a weapon is out of ammunition, it is purged so that Dendoh can fight with a lighter body. It was probably made with a hint taken from the line Hokuto said when he first rode Dendoh: "Don't you have any weapons? Like missiles, or beams, or swords, or bows, or yo-yos?"
uncertain: [jp]...[jp] kept as a hedge ("seems to have been made, probably...")

36.en: A giant robot brought from outer space as a legacy of the planet Alktos. Its Japanese name, GEAR Senshi Dendo, is read "Gear Fighter Dendoh." It operates through a cockpit mechanism that traces the pilots' movements and through programs installed by the Gear Commanders. It requires two chosen pilots, and nobody else can operate it. Incidentally, Ginga rides in the right chest and Hokuto in the left chest. A major external feature is the four Hyper Plasma Drives mounted on its hands and feet, and it can unleash many special moves by using these turbines. It is powered by Hyper Dendoh Batteries and can also fly on its own through the effect of anti-magnetic lines of force, but when the batteries run out, the Gear stops functioning. On its own, Dendoh carries no firearms at all and is a melee-only machine, fighting with the movements of Ginga's Shorinji Kempo. However, by file-saving data weapons it can use weapons, and its combat power increases several times over. Each data weapon also has its own special move, a Final Attack, but these moves use up the batteries heavily and have the drawback of leaving them empty after a single shot.
uncertain: Title reading: the text says [jp] is read [jp]; rendered "GEAR Senshi Dendo" read "Gear Fighter Dendoh"
[jp] rendered "anti-magnetic lines of force"

38.name_jp: 電童・ガトリングボア
38.en: Dendoh equipped with Gatling Boar. Its Final Attack is a Gatling cannon that fires countless beam shots. The ability unlocked by Gatling Boar is Clock Manager, which can stop the time of targets within a limited field. Because it is such a convenient ability, Ginga used it often.

40.name_jp: 電童・ドラゴンフレア
40.en: Dendoh equipped with Dragon Flare. Its Final Attack is a dragon of flame that burns the enemy to ashes. The ability unlocked by Dragon Flare is Crush Ray, a destructive ray that destroys computer circuits. It has no physical destructive power, but it was extremely effective against the Gulfer, who are machine life forms.

41.name_jp: 電童・バイパーウィップ
41.en: Dendoh equipped with Viper Whip. Its Final Attack is to throw a plasma sphere created by spinning the wire. The ability unlocked by Viper Whip is Illusion Flash, which is super-speed movement that leaves afterimages.

42.name_jp: 電童・フェニックスエール
42.en: Dendoh equipped with Phoenix Alae. Its Final Attack is a rainbow-colored light that destroys all machines. The ability unlocked by Phoenix Alae is Infinite Layer, which allows unlimited energy to be supplied to Dendoh.

43.en: Dendoh equipped with Bull Horn. Its Final Attack is to split the ground with a fist and make it rise up like a sword to pierce the enemy. The ability unlocked by Bull Horn is Auto Pressure, which allows the turbines to form a gravity field. Perhaps because Ginga could not make good use of gravity control, it was seldom used.
uncertain: [jp] rendered as a speculation about Ginga

45.name_jp: 電童・ユニコーンドリル
45.en: Dendoh equipped with Unicorn Drill. Its Final Attack is a drill-shaped tornado shot. The ability unlocked by Unicorn Drill is Firewall, a transparent plate-shaped barrier. Perhaps because it was the first data weapon Hokuto saved, he is strongly attached to it, and it was the one used most often. Note that, unlike in the game, in the original work the special abilities of the data weapons saved in the Gear Commanders could be used regardless of Dendoh's form.

46.en: Dendoh equipped with Leo Circle. Its Final Attack is a disc-shaped cutter of light fired with a kicking motion. The ability unlocked by Leo Circle is Hyper Scan, which makes it possible to see through an opponent and search for weaknesses. It is the data weapon Ginga is most attached to, and although he used it often, the Hyper Scan ability was not put to much use.

48.en: Dendoh equipped with Kiba. When Dendoh uses it, it becomes Kiba Striker. Its Final Attack is a charging move with a spinning drill. Unlike the other Final Attacks, it is not a type that fires something, but its power is correspondingly enormous. It also helps that it holds the power of two.
uncertain: [jp] rendered "the power of two" (two data weapons, Unicorn Drill and Leo Circle)

50.en: A buffalo-type data weapon that symbolizes "Wisdom." It is usually quiet, but when angered it is out of control. It is the strongest of the data weapons. For some reason it was not used much. Its attribute is "Earth."

51.en: A unicorn-type data weapon that symbolizes "Trust." It has a curious, friendly personality. Besides becoming a weapon or materializing, data weapons can also become "aliased," taking an astral form that has no physical interference with other objects. Unicorn Drill liked to alias and would slip out of the Gear Commander on its own to play. Its attribute is "Whirl."

52.en: A lion-type data weapon that symbolizes "Courage." It has an easygoing, slow-paced personality and often dozes off. It likes girls, becoming friends with Otome and helping with the e-mail exchanges with Yuki-chan of C-DRiVE. Its attribute is "Wind."
uncertain: Whose e-mail exchanges: the text does not name the person helped; presumably Ginga (JA Wikipedia says Leo Circle mediated), left as "the e-mail exchanges"

53.en: The dedicated motorcycle of Vega, deputy commander of the Earth defense organization GEAR. Designed by Dr. Inoue, it is a super bike that handles everything from directing operations at the front lines to combat. It can also transform into a water-running mode.

55.name_jp: エステバリスＣ・イズミ
55.en: Aestivalis Custom for Izumi's exclusive use. Its specs are the same as Ryoko's machine, but the head design is the same as the one Izumi rode in the days of the old Nadesico.

56.name_jp: エステバリスＣ・ヒカル
56.en: Aestivalis Custom for Hikaru's exclusive use. Its specs are the same as Ryoko's machine, but the head design is the same as the one Hikaru rode in the days of the old Nadesico.

57.name_jp: エステバリスＣ・リョーコ
57.en: An Aestivalis custom-made for Ryoko. It is a special version built on Ryoko's proposal that if two gravity wave units were attached to the back, the output would double as well. Using the high output from twice the normal number of gravity wave units, it can use a large rail cannon, and its mobility is also much improved, but it has become a machine that requires considerable skill to handle. The antenna on the head of Ryoko's machine is a reinforced sensor for commanders.

58.name_jp: 高機動型ブラックサレナ
58.en: The high-mobility form of Black Sarana. This is the state with the high-mobility unit attached, and in this form solo Boson Jump is possible. However, it cannot use its handgun and effectively has no means of attack other than ramming, so it is used only for limited operations such as breaking through enemy lines.

59.en: The name Black Sarana is given to Akito's dedicated Aestivalis when thick armor and boosters are attached to it. It is a machine Nergal prepared for Akito, who acts alone for the sake of revenge. Nozzles built into various parts of the body make acrobatic high mobility possible, but as a result of pursuing mobility and heavy armor, its armament is kept to a minimum. Therefore its greatest attack is a ramming attack that makes use of its sturdiness. The tail-shaped tail binder is a manipulator arm, and has an anchor claw at its tip.

60.name_jp: エステバリスＣ・アキト
60.en: An Aestivalis customized for Akito's exclusive use. Some say it is a prototype of the Alstroemeria. Because it was designed on the premise of attaching armor and boosters to make the Black Sarana, the wired punch and the wheels for roller dash in the heels are omitted.
uncertain: [jp] rendered "wired punch" (SRW wiki calls it "wire punch")

61.name_jp: Ｓエステバリス・サブロウタ
61.en: An Aestivalis with reinforced armament and output, commonly known as the Super Aestivalis. It is a powered-up version of the machine used exclusively by Akatsuki during the Jovian War. Aestivalis is the general name for a series of close-combat humanoid weapons developed by Nergal Heavy Industries, and by swapping various frames it can adapt to any battlefield. Also, because it has no generator of its own and operates by receiving a gravity beam from a battleship, it is small yet high-output. However, its control uses an IFS (Image Feedback System), and pilots must be injected with IFS nanomachines, so many people dislike it. In fact, after the end of the Jovian War, machines made by the Crimson Group, which do not require nanomachine injection, were officially adopted, but a small number of pilots still use customized Aestivalis.
uncertain: [jp] rendered "the Jovian War" (literal: Lizard War)
The entry name is Saburota's Super Aestivalis (Akatsuki's earlier machine is referred to in the text)

62.en: A Nadesico-class second-generation space battleship built by Nergal Heavy Industries. Because it is a test ship intended to collect operational data for a one-man-operation battleship, it can be operated by Ruri and Omoikane alone. It is equipped with two phase transition engines and four nuclear pulse engines, and can form a distortion field of higher output than the old Nadesico.

63.en: A Nadesico-class third-generation battleship secretly built at Nergal's lunar dock, equipped with a more complete one-man operation system based on Nadesico B's data. A A-Class Jumper is required, but it is a super-high-performance ship capable of solo Boson Jump without going through a Chulip. Also, its powerful sensors and communication functions allow it to infiltrate and seize enemy computer systems, but this owes less to the ship's own ability than to the ability of Ruri and Omoikane, who have a record of seizing control of Sarutahiko during the Jovian War.
uncertain: Sarutahiko: not found in any English source; kept as romanized name
[jp] rendered "Chulip" (the Jovian dimensional leap gate)

127.en: A Hakke robot bearing the title of "Heavens." Its power is the greatest among the Hakke robots. It was built by Tekkoryu but was stolen after completion. It was then secretly placed under the control of the Japanese government, but with Tekkoryu's start of activity it became a target for recapture. It has no optional equipment at all, and fights with beams and shock waves fired from the light spheres on the backs of its hands, and with melee combat. Its finishing move, the "Hades Attack," fired by bringing the light spheres on its chest and both arms together in front of the chest, has the power to break down every atom. It can also deploy a high-output barrier, making it a machine well balanced in both offense and defense. Each Hakke robot can only be piloted by a specific person, but Zeorymer is a special machine that requires two people: main pilot Masato Akitsu and sub-pilot Miku Himuro. However, Miku is only support, and only Masato can pilot it. Masato alone can also move it, but its power drops. It is housed in the hangar of the Japanese government's secret base "Last Guardian," beneath the Aokigahara sea of trees, in a state divided into four parts: the chest light sphere, upper torso, both arms, and lower body.
uncertain: [jp] rendered "Hades Attack" (SRW wiki term; romaji Meioh Attack)

128.en: Zeorymer without Miku aboard. Because Miku was taken away by Tekkoryu, Masato alone boarded it and fought Rose C'est la vie. The light in the chest light sphere has gone out, and it can only produce less than one third of its original power.

215.en: Falguen, the dedicated metal armor of Captain Meio Plato, fitted with a MAFFU flight unit. Falguen can be called a prototype of the Dragonar, and is Giganos's newest machine, designed and developed by Dr. Lang Plato, Meio's father. However, because it has a high generator output, it is a touchy machine that requires considerable skill to pilot. It can be said that only Meio, known as the Blue Hawk of Giganos, could handle it. Also worth noting is that it uses Shimour Type-A passive armor, a reversible elastic metal close to hard rubber, as its armor, which allows flexible movement.
215.notes: Batch label was [jp] ([jp]); corrected to [jp] ([jp]) per the orchestrator's fix_B.txt. Cross-series entry: translated with the best researched names; please reconcile with the group that owns the series.
uncertain: Names from Dragonar (Meio Plato, Lang Plato, Falguen, MAFFU, Giganos) taken from Wikipedia/Akurasu; Japanese [jp] is Maiyo (Akurasu episode list uses "Maio")
[jp] rendered "Shimour Type-A passive armor"; no English source found
[jp] is called "Captain" ([jp]) in the text; rank as written

216.name_jp: ヤクト・ゲルフ・マッフ
216.en: Jagd Gelf, a long-range support metal armor, fitted with a MAFFU unit. To counter the Dragonars, which excel at three-unit formation attacks, Giganos refitted the Gelf and developed the heavy-artillery Jagd Gelf and the electronic-warfare Reb Gelf. Besides Welner's machine of the Practice Squad, the Jagd Gelf was also used by Chender of Gelbock's unit.

The state combined with Gunzar is called Gandora, and the state combined with Gelfar is called Geldora. In both forms it was often used for parachute drop operations.

For high-speed flight, it can fold its legs into a flight form to reduce air resistance. Compared with its sibling machine Schwarg, Dauzehn emphasizes attack power and has the role of an attack aircraft.

It is suited to underwater combat, and has a spherical Attack Mode and a humanoid Standing Mode, and can also close its shutters completely to take a defensive form. After Allenby was rescued, Wong rode in it. It is also equipped with the Berserker System, further strengthened by the influence of the DG Cells.

It is suited to aerial combat and can transform between Attack Mode, a bird-shaped flight form, and humanoid Standing Mode. Because of the DG Cells it has an abnormal regeneration ability. It favors hit-and-run tactics that take advantage of its high speed, and its finishing move has also been upgraded from the "Silver Foot" to the "Rainbow Foot."

A machine suited to land combat, it can transform between a four-legged beast Attack Mode and a humanoid Standing Mode. It is based on the main power furnace of the Neo Japan colony and combines the abilities of all four Heavenly Kings. It is a monster that regenerated even after being defeated by the Shuffle Alliance Fist. Major Urube, infected with DG Cells, boarded it and challenged Domon and the others to a final battle.

It is the base machine of the Death series that the Devil Gundam produces, and there are many variations, such as flying and underwater types. Its weapon is a club-shaped beam rifle that can be used for both melee and shooting.

It has a peculiar shape: an upper body of the same lineage as Shining Gundam and a lower body formed by a giant transformed head. The DG Cells that make up its body inherit the three great theories of the Ultimate Cell, and through terrifying self-replication it absorbs all living things and machines and turns them into DG. Its weapons are enormous extendable claws deployed from both shoulders and beams fired from various parts of its body, and it has overwhelming power. Human spirit is essential for the Devil Gundam to display its true power, and Rain was incorporated as the human best suited to be the living unit.

231.en: A mass-produced version of the Great Mazinger that appears in Gosaku Ota's manga version of "Great Mazinger." Shinsuminichi Heavy Industries, which had developed the humanoid weapon GMFA-1, obtained the blueprints of the Great Mazinger by illegal means and built it. Its appearance and performance are basically the same as the original, but the mass-produced type has a number marked on its chest. Also, in the work, in order to distinguish the original from the mass-produced type, Boss painted "Ganso" (Original) on the waist of Tetsuya's Great Mazinger. Besides these, there is one mass-produced Great Mazinger with an all-black body.

239.en: The strongest robot of the Hyakki Empire, manufactured at a secret underground base on Izu Oshima. It was planned to be a combination of six units: Mecha Raidenki, Mecha Renmaki, Mecha Ankyuki, Mecha Kokoki, Mecha Raijuki and Mecha Tenppoki, but because Mecha Raidenki, which sortied to intercept Getter Robo that had flown to Oshima, was destroyed, it became a five-unit combination. General Hidler and Dr. Gura personally boarded it. It has overwhelming firepower and power, including beams from the eyes and drill, flame from the mouth, and missiles on the chest. It can also separate into the individual Hyakki robots. After the separated Hyakki robots were destroyed and its power dropped, it was defeated by Shine Spark.

It has a variety of weapons, such as a strange ray from its eyes and beams from its horn. It took Genki, Michiru's younger brother, hostage, but he was rescued thanks to Hayato's quick wits, and it was defeated by the tremendous power of Getter Dragon.

It was scheduled to be mounted on Mecha Yousaiki, but Dairinki, burning to avenge the Hundred Demons who had been defeated up to then, ran ahead and challenged Getter Robo alone. Its weapons are the missiles on both shoulders and the spiked large wheels fitted to both hands. The large wheels can also be used as strong shields. It gave Getter Dragon and Liger a hard time, but Getter Poseidon caught the large wheel, and it was destroyed by Getter Cyclone and Strong Missile.

Mecha Tairinki and Mecha Hangetsuki are built into the left and right wings, and it was designed to carry 200 fighters and 100 bombers. It launched from Battleship Island while Getter Robo was fighting Mecha Tairinki, and left the Saotome Institute half destroyed. It attacks with missiles fired from its shoulders and by ramming with the auxiliary wings it extends after its wings are destroyed. It was defeated by Getter Dragon's new finishing move, Shine Spark.

It took TFO hostage but was easily rescued, and was defeated by the overwhelming power of Grendizer. After transforming into humanoid form, it uses the saucer as a shield, fires a powerful destruction beam, and extends the whip-like fingers on its right hand to entangle Grendizer.

12.en: A production-model Evangelion that follows EVA-02. It is piloted by Toji Suzuhara, who was chosen as the Fourth Child. It was shipped from NERV's 1st Branch in the United States to Japan, and during an activation test at the Second Experimental Site in Matsushiro, it was taken over by the 13th Angel Bardiel with Toji still inside. Incidentally, the reason its designation is written with the plain numeral 3 rather than with the formal kanji numeral for three, as the other units' designations are, is that this unit was built in the United States.

13.en: Its official name is Multipurpose Humanoid Decisive Weapon, Artificial Human EVA-01. The special agency NERV spent 14 years and an enormous budget building the Evangelions as weapons for intercepting the Angels, and Unit-01 is the test type. It has an absolute domain and physical barrier called the AT Field (Absolute Terror Field), and it is operated by pilots called Children, boys and girls aged 14. It runs on power supplied from the outside through an umbilical cable, and in an emergency the cable can be disconnected (in this case the active limit time is about 5 minutes). Unit-01, piloted by Shinji Ikari, has many mysterious aspects even compared with the other Evas, such as restarting after passing its active limit and going berserk. It also has a red sphere called a core (a similar object has been confirmed in the Angels as well). Also, the Magoroku-E Sword exists only as a design concept and is a weapon that never appears in the anime.

15.en: The first Evangelion ever built. It can be called the prototype of machines such as Unit-01 and Unit-02. Apparently it was never intended for combat deployment, so it does not support the various equipment options. Also, because it went berserk during an activation test, it had been frozen with special Bakelite. Incidentally, it seems that many units were built before this Unit-00, the one that actually functioned.
uncertain: Last sentence: 'build up to the machine that actually activates' - interpreted as many earlier units being built before the working Unit-00.

16.en: EVA-00 that was heavily damaged in Operation Yashima and then refitted with the same armament as the other Evas. At that time its color scheme was changed to blue. Perhaps because its base frame is the experimental Unit-00, it had few chances to fight at the front and was often assigned to rear support. In the anime it was damaged in the battle with the 16th Angel Armisael, and no sorties after that have been confirmed.

17.en: A production-model Evangelion built from the data of Unit-00 and Unit-01. It is the first Evangelion designed with combat deployment in mind. It was designed in Japan, and the final assembly and activation tests were carried out in Germany. In Asuka's words, "the real Evangelion." Its true ability was shown to the fullest in the battle against the nine Mass Production Evangelions in the theatrical film, but...

18.en: EVA-01 in a berserk state. The berserk state is a mysterious behavior seen only in EVA-01. It is triggered mainly in desperate situations, and even Shinji, the pilot, cannot control it. In the berserk state Unit-01 is ferocious and destroys its enemies thoroughly. It also displays regenerative ability, and has even restored a severed arm by itself. In episode 18 of the TV series, it seems that Unit-01 was made to go berserk deliberately by a Dummy System that imitated Rei Ayanami's personality.
