79.en: The state in which the Gundam Mk-II and the G-Defenser have combined. It makes up for the Gundam Mk-II's weakness, its fragile armor, and strengthens firepower by using the Long Rifle, the main gun of the G-Defenser. It can also combine with the Mk-II while the G-Defenser stays in its aircraft form, and that configuration is called the G-Flyer (it does not appear in the game). Also, in Super Gundam form the G-Defenser's Core Fighter is separated, so it is a one-seater.
uncertain: 'G-Defenser form' (G[jp]) rendered as the G-Defenser staying in its aircraft form.

80.en: A prototype transformable mobile suit that the AEUG had Anaheim Electronics develop. It was a major milestone of the Z Project, Anaheim's new mobile suit development program, and it is a famous masterpiece that produced derivative machines such as the Hyaku Shiki and the Methuss during prototyping, and successors such as the Zeta Plus, the ZZ Gundam and the Re-GZ. It was completed by combining the movable frame technology obtained from the Gundam Mk-II, the armor material of the Rick Dias, and ideas proposed by Kamille (such as the Mk-II's flying armor). By transforming into Waverider form, it can enter the atmosphere without options such as a ballute system, and can also fly within the atmosphere. In mobile suit form as well it has high mobility and maneuverability, and thanks to its high-output generator it can also use powerful weapons such as the Hyper Mega Launcher. Later a Bio Sensor was introduced, and the machine's responsiveness improved greatly. Judau piloted it in the early part of "Mobile Suit Gundam ZZ," and even after the ZZ Gundam appeared he used this machine in situations that called for mobility.

81.en: The high-speed mobile form of the Zeta Gundam. By transforming, it concentrates the direction of its verniers toward the rear and obtains tremendous mobility. This high thrust also allows it to fly within the atmosphere. The biggest merit of transforming into this form is that atmospheric entry becomes possible without optional equipment such as a ballute system. Thanks to this function, the Zeta Gundam came to occupy an important position strategically as well. There also seems to be a variation called the "Wave Shooter," in which the flying armor is swapped for something else.

82.en: A prototype mobile suit developed by Anaheim Electronics and operated by the AEUG. Its developer is Dr. M. Nagano. It was developed as a transformable mobile suit as part of the Z Project, Anaheim's new mobile suit development program, but a structural defect was discovered and the transformation mechanism was omitted. Even so, its machine performance was high, and it was judged fully usable in actual combat, so it was assigned to the Argama. Its greatest feature is its gold armor, which apparently also had anti-beam coating ability. Furthermore, the "hyaku" (one hundred) in its name also carries the meaning of "a mobile suit that lasts a hundred years." With a high-output generator that can run the optional Mega Bazooka Launcher on its own, the high mobility given by the flexible binders on its back, and Quattro's piloting skill, it achieved great results, starting with the assault on Jaburo. It was heavily damaged in the final battle with Haman, but in "Mobile Suit Gundam ZZ" a second unit was assigned to the Argama and was mainly piloted by Beecha.
uncertain: 'Flexible binder' ([jp]) is a literal rendering; Gundam wiki calls them flexible binders/wing binders.

83.en: One of the plans for strengthening the armament of the Hyaku Shiki Kai. It mounts both beam weapons and ballistic weapons on the main body to improve firepower, and at the same time its defense is strengthened by the reflector panels on the chest. In reality, large transformable mobile suits came into their heyday, and it was never mass-produced.

84.en: An ultra-high-performance machine developed on the base of the MSK-008 Dijeh. Although the details are unknown, various revolutionary functions have been added, and it apparently may be called a completely different machine. This can also be inferred from the fact that the Dijeh SE-R's model number, SE.DJ-1R, is unique and unlike any other.

85.en: A Neo Zeon prototype mobile suit exclusively for Newtypes, improved from Haman's prototype unit 1. The prototype unit 2, with a black color scheme, is piloted by Ple. The main improvement is that the beam saber that doubles as a beam gun has become a three-pronged type, giving a slight increase in offensive power; its basic performance is equal to that of prototype unit 1.

86.en: A Neo Zeon prototype mobile suit exclusively for Newtypes, improved from Haman's prototype unit 1. The prototype unit 3, with a red color scheme, is piloted by Ple Two. The difference from unit 2 is that it is equipped with a psycommu controller that allows external operation, and its basic performance is equal to that of prototype units 1 and 2.

87.en: A prototype transformable heavy mobile suit that the AEUG had Anaheim Electronics develop. It was completed in Anaheim's Z Project after the Zeta Gundam. Its development concept is "an RX-78 and G-Armor that can operate alone." For that reason it inherits the transformation system built for the Zeta Gundam and the core block system and G-Parts mechanism of the RX-78 Gundam, and is made up of a Core Fighter, a Core Top forming the upper body, and a Core Base forming the lower body. Furthermore, each can be operated as a fighter, and in the combined state it can transform into the heavy fighter-bomber G-Fortress. It also emphasizes firepower, carrying many high-output beam weapons, starting with the High Mega Cannon on its forehead. On the other hand, it has the drawback of a short operating time because it consumes a great deal of energy. Among the mobile suits of around U.C. 0087 that pursued high output, it can be called the highest point reached. Judau Ashta piloted it and became the core of the Gundam Team.
uncertain: 'High Mega Cannon' follows the Gundam wiki; the older official spelling is 'Hi-Mega Cannon'.

88.en: The heavy fighter-bomber form into which the ZZ Gundam transforms. It is made up of the Core Top (the ZZ Gundam's A-Part and a Core Fighter) and the Core Base (the ZZ Gundam's B-Part and a Core Fighter), and is mainly used for long-distance travel. The ZZ Gundam was developed on the concept of handling an RX-78 Gundam and a G-Armor with a single machine, but the G-Fortress was not given as much versatility as the G-Armor. However, its attack power was the strongest around U.C. 0087.

89.en: A powerful battleship built by Anaheim Electronics on the basis of the Argama. "Nahel Argama" means "close to the Argama." It has five catapults for mobile suits and a main gun on the level of a colony laser. Also, thanks to computer support, each gun can be operated from the bridge, so it can be run with a very small crew.

90.en: A mobile suit support machine developed by Anaheim Electronics. It inherits the design philosophy of the self-propelled mobile suit gun platforms that existed in the One Year War, and can be operated as a sub-flight system armed with powerful weapons. It also has simple living quarters, so it can be used as a mobile base for long operations. It was used when the Gundam Team, who had descended to Earth, acted separately from the Argama.

91.en: A mobile suit for Newtypes that Anaheim Electronics developed with its full strength at the request of the Earth Federation Forces' Londo Bell unit. The pilot, Amuro, took part in the design himself, and it is an ultra-high-performance machine that can be called the culmination of all the Gundams to date. By using the new material psycho-frame, brought by Neo Zeon leader Char Aznable, around the cockpit and in the drive system, it boasts outstanding responsiveness and maneuverability. The psycho-frame also controls the machine's greatest feature, the Fin Funnels, psycommu-applied weapons installed for the first time on a Gundam-type mobile suit. Compared with conventional funnels, the Fin Funnels are larger and higher-output; besides being used as mega particle cannons, combining several of them generates a magnetic field and makes it possible to deploy a beam barrier. It is also well balanced in its other armament, carrying beam weapons, ballistic weapons and close-combat weapons. It fought a deadly battle with Char's Sazabi on the falling Axis, and afterward, in order to stop Axis from falling, it formed a mysterious force field through the resonance of the psycho-frame. Taking its armament, machine performance and pilot Amuro's skill together, it is no exaggeration to call it the strongest Gundam.

92.en: The mobile armor form in which the Re-GZ is equipped with the Back Weapon System. Mobility, long-range cruising ability and firepower are dramatically improved. However, the Back Weapon System is used in a nearly disposable manner, and re-equipping it (on the battlefield) after it has been detached and the machine has become a mobile suit is impossible.

93.en: A prototype mobile suit developed by Anaheim Electronics and used by the Londo Bell unit. It is a simplified mass-production prototype of the Zeta Gundam, and by being equipped with the Back Weapon System it becomes a mobile armor. This mechanism succeeded in improving producibility while maintaining high machine performance. Even so, it was far more expensive than other mass-produced machines, and its deployment ended with a single unit in the Londo Bell unit. Incidentally, Re-GZ is short for "Refined Gundam Zeta."

134.en: A VTOL aircraft that Haruka Shitow used to infiltrate TOKYO JUPITER ahead of the start of Operation Overlord. It is equipped with TDDU, an absolute barrier penetration system. It was also used when she escaped from TOKYO JUPITER together with Ayato, but it was guided to RahXephon and sank into the spring that spreads across the Room of Rah.

135.name_jp: ヴァーミリオン（エルフィ機）
135.en: A new TERRA weapon. It was brought into TERRA from the Bahbem Foundation and assigned to Alpha Squadron. Since only one unit was deployed at first, Elvy, the squadron leader, became its pilot. Unlike RahXephon, which only Ayato can ride, its cockpit is built very much like the Shinsei's, so even ordinary pilots can operate it with training. It has a weapon called the "Bausgazal" that can fire a railgun and wave-light bullets, and its power is such that a single shot blows away a reef. It also has the absolute barrier penetration system TDDU built in, and can break through the TOKYO JUPITER barrier under its own power. While on standby it is housed with a dedicated maintenance arm connected to and holding the thruster section at the waist, and at launch it is shot out directly from this state. Incidentally, the internal structure of the Vermillion is completely unknown.

136.en: An Anti-D fighter of the Earth Federation air force. It is armed with high-speed missiles and boasts high maneuverability. However, because it has no effective equipment against Dolems, it often ended up supporting RahXephon. The absolute barrier penetration system TDDU can be installed. The reason the machine Elvy flies is painted red is that it is the squadron leader's machine.

[jp] rendered 'Earth Federation' per the wiki.

137.en: A giant god that awoke from the dimensional egg in the Seon Temple "Room of Rah," located under the MU Tokyo Government-General in the center of TOKYO JUPITER. It moves by synchronizing with Ayato's consciousness, and no one but Ayato can pilot it. However, it can act autonomously, attack in self-defense, and move on its own in search of Ayato. When the chest armor opens, a core appears, and it takes Ayato into its womb through the core. The inner cavern that corresponds to the cockpit is called the "Instrumentalist's Seat," and its base is filled with water called the "Spring of Oracles," with a feather-shaped chair jutting out from the spring. Incidentally, RahXephon's pilot is called an "instrumentalist" by some people. The feathers on both sides of its forehead can be opened and closed freely, and are kept closed when Ayato is not aboard or during autonomous action. RahXephon's eyes are normally red, but beneath them is a golden eyeball called the "Eye of Truth." It also has an openable visor at the brim, which can cover the eyes. It has no armament or options at all; it emits high-frequency sound from its mouth and smashes enemies with light from its palms. Because its material, structure and power source are all unknown, the Earth Federation side classifies it as Mulian Artifact Class 5A (Five-A). A giant god of many mysteries that evolves along with Ayato's mental growth.
uncertain: 'Seon Temple' and 'Spring of Oracles' are literal renderings ([jp], [jp]); 'Instrumentalist's Seat' ([jp]) likewise.
'Eye of Truth' ([jp]) literal; the text says 'eyeball' singular so kept singular.

138.name_jp: 真聖ラーゼフォン＜アヤト＞
138.en: The form born when Ayato, having reached the true heart "Yolteotl," fused with the vessel "Xephon" and the guide "Ixtli" and obtained the title of Rah. It has the ability to fill the world with sound and tune the world. It emits rainbow-colored high-frequency waves and also possesses overwhelming arm strength. The white wings are not for flying but for tuning the world. Ayato overcame various hardships and found someone he must protect, and grew mentally; he and Ixtli, who had the form of Reika Mishima, accepted each other and became one, and as a result he obtained the "title of Rah" and transformed RahXephon into Shinsei RahXephon.
uncertain: 'Shinsei' ([jp]) is kept romanized; game-coined form name.
Last sentence: subject Ayato, 'he'.

139.en: RahXephon in its awakened state. When Ayato grows mentally or falls into a pinch, its red eyes open and the Eye of Truth appears, and it displays tremendous combat power. It also occasionally activates new abilities. When the Eye of Truth opens, Ayato sometimes sees the figure of Reika Mishima, who should have died.

140.en: Experimental Unit No. 7 among the humanoid mobile weapons developed in the "Tsentr Project" being pursued within the Federation Army. Also called a TE Absorber, it is a machine that excels at close combat and melee. However, the TE Engine, which applies Terminus Energy, has many problems with power output adjustment and so on, so the drive of the joints and other parts is supplemented by batteries. Also, to allow finer output adjustment of the TE Engine and to assist machine control, DFC (Direct Feeling Control) has been introduced, and an operator wearing a special DFC suit rides along on the machine. Its model number is YTA-07RB. One unit of the same type exists, but since it is mostly meant as spare parts, it is not used for tests or combat.
uncertain: 'Experimental Unit No. 7' follows the SRW wiki (JP: [jp]7[jp], prototype unit 7).

141.name_jp: ガルムレイド・ブレイズ（Ｇ）
141.en: Experimental Unit No. 9, developed in the Tsentr Project. Its model number is YTA-09RB. It consists of a main body built from the various data obtained from Experimental Unit No. 7, and support combat mecha called "Machine Animaloids." The TE Engine has also been replaced with a new type, with improved output and stability compared with that of Unit No. 7. It can also use an energy field called the "TE Sphere," which raises its defense. There are two kinds of Machine Animaloid, the bird-type unmanned fighter "Hiou" and the wolf-type unmanned mobile weapon "Rouga," and each can operate alone, but normally they are split into parts and attached to Experimental Unit No. 9's arms, legs, shoulders, back and so on. The form with the striking weapon formed from Rouga's head on the right arm and the Wing Booster formed from Hiou on the back is called "Form G," and like Unit No. 7 it displays performance specialized for close combat and melee. The Wing Booster also improves its aerial combat ability.

142.name_jp: ガルムレイド・ブレイズ（Ｓ）
142.en: Experimental Unit No. 9, developed in the Tsentr Project. Its model number is YTA-09RB. It consists of a main body built from the various data obtained from Experimental Unit No. 7, and support combat mecha called "Machine Animaloids." The TE Engine has also been replaced with a new type, with improved output and stability compared with that of Unit No. 7. It can also use an energy field called the "TE Sphere," which raises its defense. There are two kinds of Machine Animaloid, the bird-type unmanned fighter "Hiou" and the wolf-type unmanned mobile weapon "Rouga," and each can operate alone, but normally they are split into parts and attached to Experimental Unit No. 9's arms, legs, shoulders, back and so on. The form with the shield formed from Rouga's head on the left arm and the cannon formed from Hiou on the back is called "Form S," and unlike Unit No. 7 and Form G it displays performance specialized for long-range and artillery combat. Also, through the combined use of the shield and the TE Sphere, its defense is somewhat higher than that of Form G.

143.en: Experimental Unit No. 6 among the humanoid mobile weapons developed in the "Tsentr Project" being pursued within the Federation Army. Also called a TE Absorber, it is a machine that excels at long-range and artillery combat. However, the TE Engine, which applies Terminus Energy, has many problems with power output adjustment and so on, so the drive of the joints and other parts is supplemented by batteries. Also, to allow finer output adjustment of the TE Engine and to assist machine control, DFC (Direct Feeling Control) has been introduced, and an operator wearing a special DFC suit rides along on the machine. Its model number is YTA-06BW. One unit of the same type exists, but since it is mostly meant as spare parts, it is not used for tests or combat.

144.name_jp: サーベラス・イグナイト（Ｇ）
144.en: Experimental Unit No. 8, developed in the Tsentr Project. Its model number is YTA-08BW. It consists of a main body built from the various data obtained from Experimental Unit No. 6, and an additional weapon unit, the "Ignite Parts." The TE Engine has also been replaced with a new type, with improved output and stability compared with that of Unit No. 6. It can also use an energy field called the "TE Sphere," which raises its defense. The Ignite Parts can be operated alone as unmanned fighters, but basically they are used attached to the main body of Experimental Unit No. 8. Also, the main body of Unit No. 8 transforms into Figure W, a close-combat form, and Figure B, an artillery form (the front and back of the body are reversed), giving it more versatility than Unit No. 6. The state in which the Ignite Parts are attached to Figure W is called "Form G," and it displays performance specialized for close combat.

145.name_jp: サーベラス・イグナイト（Ｓ）
145.en: Experimental Unit No. 8, developed in the Tsentr Project. Its model number is YTA-08BW. It consists of a main body built from the various data obtained from Experimental Unit No. 6, and an additional weapon unit, the "Ignite Parts." The TE Engine has also been replaced with a new type, with improved output and stability compared with that of Unit No. 6. The Ignite Parts can be operated alone as unmanned fighters, but basically they are used attached to the main body of Experimental Unit No. 8. Also, the main body of Unit No. 8 transforms into Figure W, a close-combat form, and Figure B, an artillery form (the front and back of the body are reversed), giving it more versatility than Unit No. 6. The state in which the Ignite Parts are attached to Figure B is called "Form S," and it displays performance specialized for artillery combat.
145.notes: The Japanese text of this entry omits the TE Sphere sentence found in the Form G entries; kept as is.
uncertain: Omission of the TE Sphere sentence is in the source, not a dropped sentence.

156.en: A Gyandlar Commander whose body is made of iron sand. It has the ability to change its form into any shape, and because it originally has no fixed form, it takes no damage from physical attacks. It has a will of its own, but it can also merge with others, and it powered up by merging with Bug Newman. It has weapons usable at both long and short range, such as electromagnetic irradiation and the Double Sword, but unfortunately it seems unable to use the "Electromagnetic Poison Hand Blade."
156.notes: Cross-series (Machine Robo: Revenge of Cronos, Group A territory). Batch label was Dragoon (Banpresto Originals); corrected per fix_C.txt to Iron Sand.
uncertain: Cross-series names ('Youhei Commander', 'Bug Newman', 'Double Sword', 'Electromagnetic Poison Hand Blade') are literal/unverified; reconcile with Group A.
Subject of 'merged with Bug Newman and powered up' read as Iron Sand.

210.en: A Dein customized exclusively for Captain Min. The ammunition capacity of its 50 mm hand rail gun has also been increased, but its distinctive feature is the chainsaws called Hybrid Surge mounted on both arms. Captain Min was good at a tactic of destroying the opponent's sensors with the high-heat rounds mounted on the waist and then cutting the enemy to pieces with these chainsaws.
210.notes: Cross-series (Metal Armor Dragonar). Batch label was 'Fifth Angel Ramiel'; corrected per fix_C.txt to Stark Dyne.
uncertain: Cross-series: 'Dyne' / 'Captain Min' spellings should be reconciled with Group A (SRW wiki spells it Deins; Wikipedia: Stark Deins).
'50 mm hand rail gun': the glossary weapon is the 55.6 mm Hand Rail Gun; the text says 50 mm, kept as written.

211.en: A Dauzehn customized exclusively for Lieutenant Zin. Its armament and output have also been strengthened, but it was mainly modified as an electronic warfare machine. Using the EDV antenna, it projected holograms, created decoys of itself, and deceived the enemy.
211.notes: Cross-series (Metal Armor Dragonar). Batch label was 'Thirteenth Angel Bardiel'; corrected per fix_C.txt to Stark Dautzen.
uncertain: Cross-series spellings ('Dautzen', 'Zin') to reconcile with Group A.
[jp] rendered 'Lieutenant Zin' (Wikipedia 'Zin'); could be 'Jin'.

212.en: A Dein, the close-combat metal armor of Giganos that is mainly used as a platoon leader's machine, fitted with a flight MAFFU unit. Normally it carries a multi-discharger on its back, but this was omitted in order to mount the MAFFU unit. The right eye, which retains a trace of the Gewai, is directly connected to the cockpit as a target scope. A variation, a yellow-colored Dein exclusively for Dorchenov, also appeared.
212.notes: Cross-series (Metal Armor Dragonar). Batch label was 'Fourteenth Angel Zeruel'; corrected per fix_C.txt to Dyne Muff.
uncertain: Cross-series spellings ('Muff', 'Gewei', 'Dorchenov', 'Giganos') to reconcile with Group A.

213.en: A reconnaissance metal armor of Giganos. It is the earliest metal armor that was made, and is characterized by its huge camera eye. In the early part of the war it only had to deal with combat pods, so it could fight even with this level of equipment.
213.notes: Cross-series (Metal Armor Dragonar). Batch label was 'Seventeenth Angel Tabris'; corrected per fix_C.txt to Drau.
uncertain: Cross-series spellings ('Drau', 'Giganos', 'combat pods') to reconcile with Group A.

214.name_jp: ドラグナー１型カスタム
214.en: A Dragonar-1 (D-1) that received reinforcing modifications at the hands of Dr. Lang Plato. By incorporating the know-how gained from the development of the Dragoon and the Alliance forces' own technology, its medium-range combat ability and search ability were improved, and its original close-combat ability was also powered up. The two laser swords are mounted on the left hip, and a throw-in bomb is equipped on the right hip. Also, because a gravity-field detection system was installed on the left shoulder, the shoulder bombs were reduced to a single one on the right shoulder.
214.notes: Cross-series (Metal Armor Dragonar). fix_C.txt lists no owner record for this entry; the name Dragonar-1 Custom is judged from the text, which is identical to Group A entry 71.
uncertain: Name judged from the text (identical to Group A entry 71, Dragonar-1 Custom).
'Dr. Plato' ([jp]) and 'Alliance forces' ([jp]) to reconcile with Group A.

94.name_jp: ガンダムマックスター
94.en: A heavily armored, heavily armed Mobile Fighter that is the pride of Neo America. Boxer Mode, in which the chest armor is purged and the shoulder armor is fitted over the fists like gloves, is a desperate tactic that throws away defense to double its footwork. At this time, using the thrusters inside the shoulder armor also increases the destructive power of its punches. In addition, the dedicated shield is an excellent piece of equipment: it can be ridden like a surfboard and used as a transporter for high-speed movement.

95.name_jp: ガンダムマックスターＳ
95.en: Gundam Maxter with Super Mode activated.

96.en: A Neo France Mobile Fighter that excels in reconnaissance ability and mobility. It is a swordsmanship-based machine that makes use of the specialty of its pilot, George. Its greatest feature, however, is the Rose Bits built into the cape-type shield on its left shoulder, and its special move is an attack using countless bits that are freely controlled by brain waves. The Rose Bits are a highly versatile weapon that can also be used as a barrier or as an electromagnetic net to trap enemies, and Gundam Rose carries out a gorgeous and elegant style of combat.
uncertain: Pilot 'George' = George de Sand (Georges in some sources); 'specialty' = swordsmanship (fencing), inferred from the sentence.

97.en: Gundam Rose with Super Mode activated.

98.en: The newest-model Mobile Fighter that Neo Japan had been developing for the Gundam Fight Finals. "Mobile Fighter" is the general term for the melee-centered mobile suits made for the Gundam Fight, and they are operated by transmitting the pilot's movements to the machine through the Mobile Trace System. For this reason the pilot must have the makings of a martial artist. Put another way, this means no special training is required, but in reality the damage the machine takes is also transmitted to the pilot, so it can only be handled by a true martial artist whose mind and body have both been tempered. God Gundam has a built-in energy multiplier, an enhanced version of the Shining Gundam's emotional energy conversion system, and can convert the pilot's ki into energy. The state in which the machine's performance is greatly increased by this system is called Hyper Mode, and the machine shines gold. God Gundam surpasses the Shining Gundam in every respect, and even Domon, who had handled the Shining Gundam freely, was overwhelmed by its power.
uncertain: 'Energy multiplier' (Japanese: Energy Multiplier katakana) is a literal rendering; not confirmed in an English source.
'ki' kept as a term for the pilot's inner energy.

100.en: God Gundam with the cooling fins on its back opened to release the residual heat from activating Hyper Mode. It almost looks as if it is giving off a halo.

101.en: God Gundam riding Fuunsaiki in Hyper Mode.

102.en: A Mobile Fighter of Neo China that emphasizes burst speed. It was designed on the premise that a martial artist would ride in it, and although it has fewer verniers than other Gundams, it has extremely high mobility. The twelve Feilong Flags in total, mounted on its back and both shoulders, are beam lances that generate flag-shaped beams, an all-purpose weapon that can be used for any purpose, including harassing fire. In addition, the Dragon Claws on both arms extend and retract freely and can also make flame attacks, and even the queue at the back of its head traces the pilot's movements, serving as a hidden weapon that strikes vital points when the enemy is caught off guard.
uncertain: 'Feilong Flag' spelling follows the Gundam Wiki (also seen as Fei Long Flag).
'queue' = braided pigtail (bensatsu, the Qing-style braid).

103.en: Dragon Gundam with Super Mode activated.

104.en: A Mobile Fighter of Neo Sweden. It is also the only female-type Gundam of the 13th Gundam Fight. Its armor has been pared down to the limit in favor of mobility and flexibility, and it bewilders enemies with its quick movements. Its greatest feature is the Berserker System, which forcibly draws out the pilot's fighting instinct and makes her display 120% of her combat ability; when Berserker Mode is activated, the parts corresponding to its hair, the cooling fins, are deployed. After fighting and losing to Domon, she no longer used the Berserker System and instead learned the Double God Finger, but it is unclear whether the God Finger's capability was added to the Nobel Gundam.
uncertain: 'her/she' for the pilot (Allenby, female per Gundam Wiki); the original does not name the pilot in this entry.
Subject of 'fighting and losing to Domon' restored as the pilot (Allenby).

105.en: A Mobile Horse operated by Fuunsaiki, Master Asia's beloved horse. Originally a support unit for Master Gundam, it can transform into a carrier for breaking through the atmosphere.
uncertain: 'Mobile Horse' follows the Gundam Wiki ('mobile horse').

106.en: A heavyweight Mobile Fighter of Neo Russia that pursues striking power over mobility. It was built as a result of capturing and studying machines of other nations, and it has independent-drive Viktor Engines built into various parts of its body, giving it a total output twice that of an ordinary Mobile Fighter. For that reason, although it is heavily armored, it is also capable of high mobility that does not match its rugged design. The Graviton Hammer, which swings an iron ball mounted on its left shoulder, is a pure mass weapon and therefore cannot be defended against.
uncertain: 'Viktor Engine' is a literal rendering of the katakana (Victor/Viktor); the Gundam Wiki mentions a Viktor engine but spelling not fully confirmed.

107.en: Bolt Gundam with Super Mode activated.

108.en: A Mobile Fighter of Neo Nepal. Its prayer-bead-like arms and waist allow quite flexible movement. In place of legs it is equipped with high-output thrusters and moves through the air as if sliding. It also has a transformation mechanism to a defensive form in which the waist and chest are stored in its bell-shaped lower body.
uncertain: Gundam Wiki lists this machine as 'Mandor Gundam (aka Mandala Gundam)'; 'Mandala Gundam' kept to match the game.

109.en: A military Mobile Fighter of Neo Japan. It is a sibling machine of the Shining Gundam and was meant to be used by Major Urube in the fight against the Devil Gundam. The armor on both shoulders attaches to the Beam Bow on its left hand to become the Rising Shield. Its basic performance is equal to the Shining Gundam's, but it has no Super Mode, and its machine tuning is set for weapon combat rather than melee combat.
uncertain: 'Major Ulube' - rank taken from the pilot entry (Ulube Ishikawa, major).

110.en: A new female-type partner robot for Mazinger Z that replaces the destroyed Aphrodite A. A motorcycle called the Scarlet Mobile docks with its head and becomes the cockpit. Compared with Aphrodite A, its combat strength has been improved because it was developed from the start for the purpose of fighting the Mechanical Beasts, but a cockpit consisting only of the Scarlet Mobile (the motorcycle) is, in a sense, even more dangerous than Boss Borot.

111.en: A robot that Boss forced the three Photon Power Laboratory scientists to build. It is made from scrap, but there were times when it showed that it could help Mazinger Z and Great Mazinger. In addition, various enhancement modifications were made depending on the situation, on Boss's ideas.
uncertain: 'three Photon Power Laboratory scientists' = the three scientists (Mazinger wiki: 'Three Scientists').

112.en: A super robot completed by Dr. Juzo Kabuto over fifteen years. However, the doctor was assassinated by the Iron Mask sent by Baron Ashura, and Mazinger Z was entrusted to his grandson Koji. It uses Photon Power energy, and its armor is made of Super Alloy Z, refined from Japanium ore. It is equipped with various weapons over its whole body, and its combat strength is said to rival the U.S. Seventh Fleet. It could not fly on its own, but it later overcame that weakness by combining with the Jet Scrander, the Crimson Wings. The Jet Scrander has variable wings, which sweep back when flying at high speed of Mach 2.3 or more. Like Mazinger, the Scrander is also made of Super Alloy Z and has built-in weapons such as the Southern Cross Knives. In addition, it has a kind of overboost mechanism called Mazin Power, which was used when in a pinch.
uncertain: 'Iron Mask' (tetsukamen) is a mask-wearing assassin; English name per Mazinger Wiki ('Iron Mask Captain') not fully matching, kept as 'the Iron Mask'.

113.en: A combat super robot that Dr. Kenzo Kabuto, who predicted the Mycenae Empire's invasion of the surface, developed using the basic design of Mazinger Z as a base. It uses Photon Power energy, and its armor is made of Super Alloy New Z. It is piloted by the small fighter Brain Condor performing a Fire On onto Great Mazinger. In addition, the retractable wings built into its back, the Scramble Dash, allow it to fly at Mach 4. Much of its armament shares Mazinger Z's concept, but it is equipped with distinctive weapons: the Mazinger Blade, which is effective in close combat, and the ultra-high-voltage discharge Thunder Break. Later, the Great Booster was developed with the aim of improving its mobility and attack power. Its weak point is the Scramble Dash storage section, and if it is attacked there, all functions are paralyzed for an instant.
uncertain: 'Fire On' (docking command) kept as written in the game.
'Mach 4' / Scramble Dash per Mazinger wiki.

114.en: A female-type combat robot that Dr. Kenzo Kabuto, who predicted the Mycenae Empire's invasion of the surface, developed as a partner for Great Mazinger. Its control craft is the small fighter Queen Star. Because it was developed for combat from the start, it has enough power to stand up to the Warrior Beasts. It can also fly thanks to the Venus Scrander, which was developed later.
uncertain: 'Queen Star' is a literal rendering of the control craft name; not verified in an English source.

115.en: The mass-produced version of Great Mazinger that appears in Gosaku Ota's version of "Great Mazinger." It was built by Shinsuminichi Heavy Industries, which developed the humanoid weapon GMFA-1, after obtaining Great Mazinger's blueprints by illegal means. Its appearance and performance are basically no different from the original, but the mass-produced units have a number marked on the chest. Also, in the work, in order to tell the original and the mass-produced units apart, Boss wrote "Ganso" (the original) in paint on the waist of Tetsuya's Great Mazinger. Besides these, there is also one all-black mass-produced Great Mazinger.
uncertain: Company name: 'Shinsuminichi' per Mazinger wiki; entry 116 writes it with the kanji in a different order (possible typo in the game).
'GMFA1' rendered 'GMFA-1' (hyphen added).
Author's name romanized 'Gosaku Ota' (Mazinger wiki: Gosaku Ota); the game's kanji reading could also be Tagosaku.

116.en: The prototype of the mass-produced Great Mazinger that appears in Gosaku Ota's version of "Great Mazinger." Unlike the other mass-produced units, its whole body is painted black, and it has no machine number either. The president of Shinsuminichi Heavy Industries had it attack Tetsuya's Great in order to give a presentation to people in the defense and intelligence fields of countries around the world. At that time it showed glimpses of power exceeding the original and overwhelmed Tetsuya. It passes into the hands of the Mycenae Empire together with the other mass-produced units, but Tetsuya and the others destroy its autopilot device, and they operate it as the "Great Corps."
uncertain: Company name written with kanji in a different order than entry 115; treated as the same company.
Subject of the last clause: 'they' = Tetsuya and the others (the units are operated by them as the Great Corps).

117.name_jp: グレートマジンガー（元祖）
117.en: The Great Mazinger in Gosaku Ota's version of "Great Mazinger," with "Ganso" (the original) written on its waist by Boss in order to tell it apart from the mass-produced Greats. Boss himself gave the reason: "There are lots of them, so this makes it easy to tell." Its performance and everything else are the same as the original.

118.en: A Getter Robo built by the Dinosaur Empire from blueprints stolen from the Saotome Institute. It is read "Getter Queen." It is piloted by Gola, the daughter of Dinosaur Emperor Gore. Because Gola had come to feel affection for humanity, she shielded Getter Robo from the attack of Mechasaurus Gin and met a tragic end, exploding and taking Gin down with her. Although it bears the Getter name, since the Dinosaur Empire uses it, it is unclear whether its power source is Getter Rays. Its weapons are also completely unknown.
uncertain: Subject restored as Gola (the scene settles it: the pilot who shielded Getter Robo).
'Mechasaurus Gin': name of the Dinosaur Empire machine; spelling per Getter Robo wiki 'Mechasauruses'.

119.en: A new-type Getter Robo developed by Dr. Saotome for combat from the start. The Getter Ray amplifier gives it ten times the power of the first Getter, and its armor newly uses Synthetic Steel G. Getter Dragon, which combines in the order Dragon, Liger, Poseidon, is mainly for aerial combat, and Ryoma continues from Getter 1 as its pilot. It boasts the highest combat strength of the three forms, and above all the later-added Shine Spark is its strongest special move.
uncertain: 'Synthetic Steel G' (gouseikou G) - no English source verified; alternative 'Composite Steel G'.
'Dragon, Liger, Poseidon' order = the combination order of the three machines.

120.en: A new-type Getter Robo developed by Dr. Saotome for combat from the start. The Getter Ray amplifier gives it ten times the power of the first Getter, and its armor newly uses Synthetic Steel G. Getter Liger, which combines in the order Liger, Poseidon, Dragon, is mainly for ground and underground combat, and Hayato is its pilot. It boasts the highest mobility of the three forms and uses Alter Ego and Mach Special. Also, its right hand is a five-fingered manipulator, but it can transform into a drill depending on the situation. Note that in the original work, Getter Liger can fly from the start as well.
uncertain: 'Alter Ego' = the game's skill name for bunshin (afterimage), kept consistent with the system-term glossary.

121.en: A new-type Getter Robo developed by Dr. Saotome for combat from the start. The Getter Ray amplifier gives it ten times the power of the first Getter, and its armor newly uses Synthetic Steel G. Getter Poseidon, which combines in the order Poseidon, Dragon, Liger, is a bipedal type, unlike Getter 3. It is mainly used in underwater combat. Also, its legs can be bent below the knee and transformed into caterpillar treads. Its pilot is Benkei, who newly joined the Getter Team in place of Musashi, who lost his life in the fight against the Dinosaur Empire. Note that in the original work it does not use Daisetsuzan Oroshi as it does in the game. It boasts the highest power of the three forms. Also, in "Getter Robo G" it was later modified so that it could fly.
uncertain: 'Daisetsuzan Oroshi' kept in romanized form (Getter Wiki spelling 'Daisetzuzan Oroshi' also seen).

122.en: A UFO Robot built by gathering the scientific power of Planet Fleed. Its pilot is Duke Fleed, and it has a self-defense system that gives an electric shock to anyone who approaches it other than a person who holds the proof of the Fleed royal family. Its armor uses Cosmic Alloy Gren, which does not exist on Earth, and its energy source is photons collected from light such as the sun's. It can combine with the support combat saucer Spazer, and with the three kinds of Earth-made Spazers built later, it can adapt to any situation. Its weapons are powerful ones, such as Space Thunder, which emits a 60,000-degree beam, and Double Harken, a giant scythe used by combining the crescent-shaped blades on both shoulders. It reached Earth with Duke and was hidden beneath the Institute of Space Science until the Vegan Empire appeared.
uncertain: 'photons' = kouryoushi (light quanta); the Mazinger wiki uses 'Photonic Energy' for the Double Spazer.

123.en: The form of Grendizer and Double Spazer combined. It is a machine that excels at aerial combat, born when the two machines combine with the shout "Combination Cross." Duke does the main piloting, but Koji operated the Double Spazer's weapons. Unlike with the Spazer, the weapons and limbs that were unusable after combining can be used freely, so there are no restrictions on movement during combat, and both flight ability and combat ability are improved. Note that although they do not appear in the game, the original work also featured the Marine Spazer for underwater use and the Drill Spazer for underground use.

124.en: The name of the support saucer mecha that strengthens Grendizer's flight ability, armament and armor, but the state combined with Grendizer is also called by this name. Like Grendizer, it has a body of Cosmic Alloy Gren, and when it combines with the shout "Spazer Cross," the seat moves to the Spazer control cockpit in front of the tail fin. Also, even when separated it can be remotely operated unmanned, fulfilling the role of assisting Grendizer. In space it is capable of hyperspace navigation; in the atmosphere it cannot reach that kind of speed, but when it flies at full power its body glows brightly and it truly becomes a UFO. Grendizer normally waits in this state in the hangar inside the Institute of Space Science, and so that the base's location would not be discovered, each time it sortied it chose one launch point from among the normal launch gate and the secret launch gates Route 1 through Route 8. Incidentally, Route 1 is a volcano crater, Route 2 a virgin forest, Route 3 an abandoned mine, Route 4 Hell Valley, Route 5 a lake, Route 6 a cave in a mountainside, Route 7 a waterfall basin, and Route 8 a factory ruin.
uncertain: Subject of the sortie sentence restored as Grendizer (in Spazer state), as the scene settles it.

125.en: A large support fighter developed by Genzo Umon. It was the first Earth-made Spazer, and in the story Koji Kabuto rode it. It combines with Grendizer depending on the situation. It was designed as a VTOL aircraft and has large rotors on both wings. The wings tilt up and down and the nose can also move like the Concorde's, so the machine's silhouette changes when landing, in flight, and when combining. Its body is made of the same Super Alloy New Z as Great Mazinger, and it is a hybrid machine whose power source uses the same photonic energy as Grendizer.

126.en: The world's first Earth-made UFO, designed by Koji Kabuto and built at NASA. At first it was not meant for combat, so it had no weapons at all, but it was later equipped with rapid-fire small missiles and a machine gun. Its maneuverability is high, and it can fight Minifos on even terms. Against Saucer Beasts it can only be called underpowered, but it was active when it counted, such as saving Grendizer when it was in a pinch.

264.en: A Hakke Robo bearing the title "Thunder," piloted by Saiga. It is the last Hakke Robo to be completed, and it is not humanoid. It is equipped with the atomic-nucleus fragmentation cannon Proton Thunder, the one weapon said to be able to counter Zeorymer, which Masaki developed. This weapon is located on both sides of the machine's central sphere and turns matter within a radius of several kilometers into fine particles. It vanishes enveloped in the light of the Hades Attack together with Burrstone.
264.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Thunder Omzack (Hades Project Zeorymer).
uncertain: Spellings Omzack / Burrstone / Saiga follow the SRW wiki and Wikipedia.
'Hades Attack' = Meioh Attack (SRW wiki uses 'Hades Attack').
'Zeorymer, which Masaki developed' kept literally (source says Masaki developed it).

265.en: A Hakke Robo bearing the title "Wind," piloted by Taiha. As its title says, it makes varied attacks using wind: "Bone Hoon," which slams down a powerful wind; "Blay Wain," which cuts with a kamaitachi (a slashing whirlwind); and "Dead Ron Hoon," which raises a giant tornado and takes away the target's freedom. It excels at aerial combat and can fly at high speed with the wings extending from over its shoulders. It pressed Zeorymer, which it was fighting for the first time, but was defeated by the Hades Attack.
265.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Wind Lanstar.
uncertain: Attack names Bone Hoon / Blay Wain / Dead Ron Hoon are transliterations (no English source found); the SRW wiki lists a 'Death Dragon Tornado' that may correspond to the third.

266.en: A Hakke Robo bearing the title "Earth," piloted by Rockfell. It was designed with the aim of destroying large cities and is not suited to close combat. It is equipped with a weapon that plants both arms on the ground and sends vibration waves to activate the magma layer and cause a great earthquake. In addition, it is equipped with anti-personnel and anti-materiel beams and missiles. It charged at Zeorymer with both arms blown off and was destroyed by a shock wave.
266.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Earth Dinodilos.

267.name_jp: 月のローズセラヴィー
267.name_en: Rose C'est La Vie of the Moon
267.en: A Hakke Robo bearing the title "Moon," piloted by Ritsu. It carries many beam weapons on its chest, legs, fingers and so on. It also used "Luna Flash," a sword made by converging the beams at its fingertips, and gave Zeorymer a hard time even in close combat. It is equipped with the special weapon "J-Kaiser," which releases all the energy the machine has, but it cannot be used continuously. For that reason it launches three satellites called the "Children of the Moon" and sends lightning energy to its own machine to recharge. It is destroyed by the Hades Attack of Zeorymer, which regained the Dimensional Coupler System and unleashed its true power.
267.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Moon Rose C'est La Vie.
uncertain: 'Children of the Moon' (Tsuki no Ko) is a literal rendering.
'Rose C'est La Vie' spelling per SRW wiki (game kana: Rose Seravy).

268.en: A Hakke Robo bearing the title "Fire," piloted by Shi-Aen. In the combination attack "Twin Lords" with Gallowin of water, piloted by his younger sister Shi-Tau, Gallowin's "Beam Searcher" and Bryst's "Plasma Light Bullet Magrash" collide in midair and destroy the target along with the space around it. There is also a technique called "Twin Flare," in which the two machines are linked and fire. As a single-machine attack it is equipped with the napalm "Flare Launcher," which gives off high heat. It cannot fly, but it can glide by hovering. It was heavily damaged shielding Gallowin from Zeorymer's beam, and was destroyed by the Hades Attack together with Gallowin.
268.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Fire Bryst.
uncertain: Pilot is the older sibling of Si Tau ('younger sister' stated in the text).
'Plasma Light Bullet Magrash' is a transliteration/literal rendering.

269.en: A Hakke Robo bearing the title "Water," piloted by Shi-Tau. Because it was developed as a support machine for Bryst, its weapons are mainly auxiliary: "Gallowin Blizzard," which seals the opponent's movement, and the "Mega Searcher," which emits laser beams. In the combination technique with Bryst, "Twin Flare," it plays the roles of energy supply, laser search and cooling. In order to secure its position when performing the combination technique, its mobility is higher than Bryst's. In the end it was destroyed together with Bryst by the Hades Attack.
269.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Water Gallowin.
uncertain: Entry 268 calls the combination attack 'Twin Lords' while this entry calls it 'Twin Flare' (both as in source).

270.en: A Hakke Robo bearing the title "Mountain," piloted by Giso. Like Dinodilos, it was designed with the aim of attacking cities. It is equipped with 500 missiles over its whole body and hides a total of 18 nuclear missiles, nine under the armor of each leg. It can glide with the boosters on its shoulders and the hover on its legs. It vanishes enveloped in the light of the Hades Attack together with Omzack.
270.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Mountain Burrstone.

271.en: The mass-produced version of Vermillion. A total of three units were assigned to TERRA, and they become the machines of Alpha Squadron members. Its performance and armament are no different from the Vermillion piloted by Elvy, and it fought mass-produced Dolems on equal or better terms.
271.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Vermillion (Green).
uncertain: 'Elvy' = Elvy Hadhiyat (RahXephon wiki); the game katakana reads Elfi.
'mass-produced Dolems' - the source says ryousangata Dolem; the RahXephon wiki describes Vermillion itself as a mass-produced Dolem.

272.en: A Dolem that takes on the duty of defending the capital, with huge wings. It fires plasma burst light from the top of its head and shot down fighter planes in Operation Overlord. It can also put up a sound barrier to defend against attacks. It seems to be under the direct command of Maya Kamina and shows up on many battlefields.
272.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Allegretto.
uncertain: 'plasma burst light' is a literal rendering of the source term.
'capital' = Tokyo presumably; the text says only 'the capital'.

273.en: A Dolem that is something like a combat commander among the Mu. Its combat strength is among the strongest even among Dolems, and its attack power is enough to defeat several of the Federation's warships in one blow. It extends its sharp claws long to pierce and slash enemies. It also hides a third arm on its right chest. It appeared before RahXephon riding on a pedestal called Brillante.
273.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Obbligato (the RahXephon wiki also writes Obligato).
uncertain: 'Federation' = Renmei ('the Alliance'); Wikipedia calls the human-side military 'the Federation'.

274.name_jp: 真聖ラーゼフォン＜クオン＞
274.en: The form of Quon, who attained Yolteotl, becoming one with the Xephon born from the black egg. It is the counterpart of Ayato's Xephon and has black wings. Like Ayato's Xephon, it has the ability to tune the world, and its physical abilities are the same. Incidentally, Quon's Ixtli was Ayato dressed in black. This is because Ayato inherited Quon's genes.
274.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: True RahXephon <Quon>.
uncertain: 'Yolteotl' is a guess at the romanization of the katakana (not found on the RahXephon wiki).
'True RahXephon <Quon>' for Shinsei RahXephon <Quon>: 'True RahXephon' is the RahXephon wiki / SRW wiki name of Ayato's final form; applying it to Quon's machine is an assumption.

275.en: A Dolem with a body like a stringed instrument. It attacked the fleet that was transporting RahXephon. It extends tentacles to entangle its target and corrode metal. It was defeated by RahXephon, and the Earth Federation took the wreckage back.
275.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Grave.
uncertain: 'Earth Federation' (Chikyuu Renmei) - exact English name unverified.

276.en: A mobile weapon of the Mu, smaller than a Dolem. They appear in countless numbers and attack with beams from slits in their upper part. TERRA called them "D2."
276.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Dotem (RahXephon wiki: Dotems, designated D-2 by TERRA).
uncertain: Source spells 'beam' with a hyphen variant; rendered 'beams'.

277.en: A Dolem that tried to manipulate Ayato's mind. With the ring above its head it swallowed RahXephon into a phase space, and by sending Dolem stones into RahXephon's mouth it made Ayato believe he was in TOKYO JUPITER. However, it was cut in two by the awakened RahXephon.
277.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Vivace.
uncertain: 'RahXephon's mouth' resolved from the RahXephon wiki (Vivace inserts a stone tube into RahXephon's mouth); the source says only 'the mouth'.
'Dolem stones' (Dolem kesseki) is a literal rendering.

278.en: A Dolem floating in the air of TOKYO JUPITER, from which Ayato Kamina is absent. They exist in countless numbers in a stationary state and have a function that, upon sensing an intruder, takes action in defense. They attack enemies by firing beams from their heads.
278.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Metronome (Red) (RahXephon wiki: Metronomes, sentry Dolems of Tokyo Jupiter).
uncertain: Tokyo Jupiter is written in Latin capitals in the game ('TOKYO JUPITER').

279.en: The strongest, largest-class Dolem, given to Kuki. Itsuki said in the strategy meeting that its total length is about 2,600 m, its mass is 10^9 t, and its destructive power is 10^27 L. The plasma beam fired from its entire underside has enough power to instantly destroy a whole city. Also, its head floats in the air.
279.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Largo.
uncertain: 'Kuki' = Masayoshi Kuki (RahXephon wiki, controls Largo). 'Itsuki' = Itsuki Kisaragi presumed (head of TERRA's science department); the kanji alone is not conclusive.
'10^9 t' and '10^27 L' written with ^ because superscripts are not allowed.

280.en: The form Medius Locus took after absorbing a massive energy convergence body and undergoing further transformation. The core section housing AI1 has itself changed form greatly, and what has become of the pilot inside is unknown.
280.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Medius Locus (later form).
uncertain: 'pilot' = occupant (noriko-sha) of the core; rendered as pilot.

281.en: The form in which the core housing AI1 grew huge through the self-repair and self-evolution abilities of the runaway Lasmunanium and fused with the TE Engine. As its name "ALL In 1" suggests, it tries to take everything into its body.
281.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: AI1.
uncertain: 'Lasmunanium' spelling per SRW wiki (Medius Locus page).

282.en: A mobile weapon created by Medius Locus. It is thought to be based on the Tergum, but details are unknown.
282.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Sinistra.
uncertain: 'Sinistra' spelled from the orchestrator's correction file (kana Shinisutora); not found on a wiki.
'Telgum' per SRW wiki (Medius Locus page).

283.en: A mobile weapon created by Medius Locus. It is thought to be based on the Frons, but details are unknown.
283.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Dextera.
uncertain: 'Dextera' spelled from the orchestrator's correction file; not found on a wiki.
'Flonnes' per SRW wiki (Medius Locus page; game katakana Furonsu / Frons).

284.en: A mysterious unmanned mobile weapon. It is said to resemble Tsentr Project prototype unit No. 1, but details are unknown.
284.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Telgum (SRW wiki: Y-Tse-P-01 Telgum).
uncertain: The SRW wiki says Medius Locus can create Telgum and Flonnes from Lasmunanium.

285.en: A mysterious unmanned mobile weapon. It is said to resemble Tsentr Project prototype unit No. 2, but details are unknown.
285.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Flonnes (SRW wiki spelling; game katakana Furonsu / Frons).
uncertain: 'Flonnes' vs 'Frons': wiki spelling used.

286.en: The Earth Federation Forces, concerned about the high attrition rate of mass-produced humanoid mobile weapons due to repeated wars, drew up a development plan for a new-concept machine looking ten years ahead, the "Tsentr Project." Dr. Mitar Zapat, the central figure of the project, built a prototype of the "TE Engine," which applied "Terminus Energy," as the power source of the prototype machines. However, although Terminus Energy has high output, collecting it and converting it to power was extremely difficult, and it was predicted that it would take several years to complete the TE Engine. In addition, Dr. Zapat had also succeeded in developing "Lasmunanium," an armor material capable of self-repair, but this too ran into the problem that its function was difficult to control, just like the TE Engine. After trial and error with prototype units No. 1 through No. 4, Dr. Zapat gave up on developing a machine equipped with both Lasmunanium and the TE Engine. He assigned Lasmunanium to prototype unit No. 5, "Medius Locus," and the TE Engine to prototype units No. 6 and No. 7, and decided to pursue and improve each function. Furthermore, these three machines were given concepts and armament assuming actual combat: prototype No. 6 was developed for high-mobility combat and artillery combat, prototype No. 7 for close combat and melee combat, and Medius Locus as a machine with performance intermediate between the two machines described above. This machine was the first of the three above to roll out, but no test pilot was decided, and unlike prototypes No. 6 and No. 7, almost no tests of various kinds were carried out (one theory holds that it secretly underwent some kind of modification). Afterwards it was seized by someone and went missing. Its model number is YTsP-05.
286.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Medius Locus (first form).
uncertain: Model number: the game shows a garbled character (kilo symbol) between Y and P; the SRW wiki gives Y-Tse-P-05 (Cyrillic Tse), written here as YTsP-05.
'Mitar Zapat' and 'Tsentr Project' per SRW wiki.
The parenthetical keeps the original hedging.

287.en: The form Medius Locus transformed into. Based on the various machine data and combat data AI1 obtained, it changed form through the self-evolution ability of Lasmunanium and powered up. Later it took in the TE Engine and became able to collect and use Terminus Energy. Compared with before the transformation, the machine's size itself changed, and its appearance and weapons lean toward those of a special machine (super robot). This is thought to be because Eldy had entered the data of Tsentr Project prototype unit No. 7 (special machine type) into AI1 in advance.
287.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Medius Locus (second form).
uncertain: 'Eldy' = Eldy Middi (SRW wiki); 'special machine (super robot)' follows the game's tokki gloss.

288.en: A Dolem with a form that closely resembles a parka. Its face floats inside the parka, and it strikes opponents with the sharp protrusions where its feet would be. Because the Vibrato is in sync with Hiroko Asahina, when Vibrato is hurt, Hiroko is hurt too. It also displayed messages Hiroko wrote in her notebook on electronic signboards and the like around the city. It was defeated by Ayato, who struggled to protect Hiroko, but that simultaneously meant Hiroko's death.
288.notes: Batch label was wrong; name_jp corrected per corrections/fix_D.txt (orchestrator). Text translated as describing the corrected machine. Corrected: Vibrato (RahXephon wiki: a Dolem bound to Hiroko Asahina, whose design reflects her pink hoodie).
uncertain: 'Mulian Vibrato' - the source label; the RahXephon wiki treats Vibrato as a Dolem bound to Hiroko.

1.en: A powerful commander who once even took the No. 1 spot in the Gyandlar Commander ranking, in place of Devil Saturn 6. Ashura fires Nattoru bullets, which rob the target of bodily freedom, from the abdomen, and specializes in destroying the immobilized opponent in cruel ways. By nature Ashura is cruel and cunning, and once set a trap by turning Rom's party's surprise attack plan against them. Ashura drove Baikanfu into a corner, but was pierced through the chest by Thunder Cyclone and defeated.
1.notes: Text identical to unit entry 157; translation reused.
uncertain: Gender of Asura unknown: no pronouns used.
'Nattoru bullet' is romanized from kana (no English source).

2.en: The boss of the space crime organization Gyandlar. Gyandlar's goal is to rule the entire universe and bring darkness and fear. It is also searching for Hyribead, an infinite energy said to grant eternal life. Gades is a villain who has wandered space for thousands of years piling up evil deeds, and trusts no one but himself. His sorcerous power is such that he can paralyze enemies in distant places. He attacked planet Cronos after Hyribead, but his ambition was thwarted by the Cronos tribe warriors, including Rom. He hates having rust form on his body to an extreme degree, and always kept with him a dedicated robot, Bibibi Mouse, to polish his body.
2.notes: Text identical to unit entry 158; translation reused.
uncertain: Gender male per ja Wikipedia/voice actors (glossary).
'Bibibi Mouse' romanized from kana.

3.en: The true form of Gyandlar executive Garudi. In truth, he is Rom and Leina's real older brother, whom they had thought dead since early childhood. He was picked up by Gades, who valued his talent for Tenku Shin Ken, and for a long time he underwent mind control as a Gyandlar executive. (The fearsome appearance of Garudi is also thought to be part of that control.) In the final episode of the original story, he gives his own sword to his beloved younger brother Rom and orders him to cut down Gades.
uncertain: 'Garudi' vs. 'Guardi' (English Wikipedia uses both).
The parenthetical refers to Garudi's armored/fearsome look; 'fearsome appearance of Garudi' is my rendering of 'ikatsui Garudi no sugata'.

4.en: A low-ranking Gyandlar Commander. When first introduced, Kyasumodon appeared as the main enemy and tried to set the Cronos tribe and the Battle tribe against each other, but after that appeared in large numbers as a grunt. Kyasumodon can transform into a flight form like a jet aircraft.
4.notes: Text identical to unit entry 159; translation reused.
uncertain: Gender unknown: 'Casmodon' repeated.

7.en: One of the Gyandlar executives. Fond of underhanded schemes and plots, Grujios serves as a kind of strategist for Gyandlar. With tremendous sorcerous power, Grujios can revive the ghosts of Gyandlar Commanders and use them as servants. In truth, the real body is only a caterpillar-like face floating in the tank of the head. Grujios was defeated by Rom in the Battle of the Heavenly Demon Castle, but, just as promised in the "I shall return" warning, came back in spirit form. After becoming a spirit, Grujios gained a new ability to take over other people's bodies, and tormented Rom's party by posing as an ally.
7.notes: Text identical to unit entry 160; translation reused.
uncertain: Gender unknown: no pronouns used.
'Battle of the Heavenly Demon Castle' is my translation of the event name.

8.en: A low-ranking Gyandlar Commander. Zarios is characterized by caterpillar-track legs, but had no especially notable role in the original story.
8.notes: Text identical to unit entry 161; translation reused.

12.en: A female Gyandlar executive. In contrast to Grujios, so to speak, she often takes direct command at the front lines. Devil Saturn 6 are her direct subordinates. Wielding an electromagnetic whip, her speech and attitude fit being called "Big Sis," but she gets angry when called that. She is bold and cruel by nature, and tries to compete with Grujios at every turn. She also has a cute side in that she is actually afraid of earthquakes, and in the original story she almost got on good terms with Tough Trailer for a moment. After that, she set a trap for Tough Trailer by making that character hold the Medusa demon sword, a cursed blade that drives its holder mad, but after that scheme failed, she herself came to favor the Medusa demon sword. She can also breathe fire from her mouth and emit hypnotic light from her eyes.
12.notes: Text identical to unit entry 162; translation reused.
uncertain: Tough Trailer's gender is not sourced, so no pronoun is used for that character.
'Big Sis' for the nickname Aneego (boss-lady / older-sister).

13.en: The combined form of Devil Saturn No. 1 through No. 6. Thanks to its viciousness and power it has held the No. 1 spot in the Gyandlar Commander ranking; it dropped in rank once, but soon came back. Its attacks are varied: not only fighting, but also flames from the mouth, claws launched on chains, beams from the eyes, and so on. It once even devised the Devil Foot Smash to counter God Hand Smash. It was often entrusted with Gyandlar's field operations, and was beaten up by Rom and the others time after time. It is a commander whose odd Kansai dialect makes it hard to hate, but in fact only Devil Saturn No. 1 actually uses the Kansai dialect, and the other five speak standard Japanese.
13.notes: Text identical to unit entry 163; translation reused.
uncertain: 'Devil Saturn' vs. English Wikipedia 'Devil Satan'.
'God Hand Smash' is a translation of the kana (Rom/Baikanfu technique).

14.en: Leina's servant, who can transform into three forms: robot, jet helicopter and supercar. Technically a member of the Jet tribe. Because Triple Jim can carry members of the Cronos tribe, Jim is a great help when traveling, but is poor at fighting because of a gentle nature. That said, Jim understands how martial artists feel, and often put Jim's own body on the line for Leina's sake. Always humble and polite in speech, Jim shouts "It is above you, if you please!" even when warning someone that something is falling from above. In episode 24, Jim performed a catchphrase imitating Rom's. Jim also seems to be able to use Tenku Chushin Ken, though only a little.
14.notes: Text identical to unit entry 1; translation reused.
uncertain: Gender unknown: 'Jim' repeated instead of a pronoun.
The line shouted ('above, if you please') is a paraphrase of the polite 'ue de gozaimasu'.

15.en: The former top disciple of Rom's father, Kirai Stol. A member of the Cronos tribe who is an elder disciple to Rom and the others. He learned Tenku Chushin Ken and surpassed his master in offensive techniques, but Kirai saw through his character, which sought only power, and did not permit him full mastery. Resenting this, he ran away from Kirai, and was living as a bandit when Gyandlar invited him, though Diondra seems to have thought he would be thrown away once he had served his purpose. He wields the forbidden technique "Tenku Chushin Ken: Electromagnetic Poison Hand-Blade." The poison hand-blade is a hand-blade into which poison has been soaked by dipping the hand in all kinds of deadly poisons; even a graze lets poison into the body through the wound and kills the opponent. He is also good at finger bullets, and has a technique called "Tenku Chushin Ken: Dark Finger Bullet."
uncertain: 'Elder disciple' for the kana wording (anideshi).
Technique names translated from the Japanese (no English source).

16.en: A low-ranking Gyandlar Commander. Its agility is its trait, but it seems not to have been depicted much in the original story.
16.notes: Text identical to unit entry 164; translation reused.

19.en: A warrior of the Jet tribe who, like Rom and Drill, trained under Kirai. He was taught Tenku Shin Ken by Kirai. As his name suggests, he can transform into a jet aircraft. Within Rom's party he is the cool, handsome type, who dashes in to rescue friends and beautiful women in their moment of crisis. He is also quite sharp, and often served as Rom's strategist. His only built-in weapon is the sword stored at his waist, from which he unleashes various secret techniques of Tenku Shin Ken. The Blazer Cannon is an additional weapon that appeared from the middle of the original story; it has the same name as Rod Drill's, but the cannon on Jet fires beams.
19.notes: Text identical to unit entry 6; translation reused.

20.en: Rom's younger sister. She goes along on Rom's journey, accompanied by Triple Jim. Although not to the degree her brother is, she has some knowledge of Tenku Chushin Ken, and has shown the Mantis Fist, the Rock-Breaking Fist and the Gale Kick. She is cheerful and active by nature, and somewhat overly devoted to her brother. For that reason, she often frets over her brother, who is popular wherever they travel. She loves fortune-telling, but no matter how many times she does it, it seems to say she is fated never to meet a wonderful person. At first she was treated like a princess, but later she rides the Power Riser and takes an active part in battle. In episode 37 she delivered a somewhat awkward catchphrase, but the catchphrase she delivered when she became the lead in a later video series was truly polished.
uncertain: 'Rock-Breaking Fist' and 'Gale Kick' are my translations of the technique names.

21.en: A fellow disciple of Rom and Jet. He is from the Battle tribe and transforms into a drill tank. Cheerful and bold, he excels at power-based fighting. He was something of a mood maker within the party, yet repeatedly saved his companions from danger with that drill. He is the type who sleeps a full 10 hours, and apparently once punched Jet in his sleep when Jet came to wake him. He has no built-in weapons, and since his trademark drill cannot be used in this form either, he fights with his fists alone, but he rarely shouts technique names; the only one confirmed is "Tenku Chushin Ken: Head-Hunting." The Blazer Cannon differs from Jet's in the shape of its muzzle, and is a missile launcher.
21.notes: Text identical to unit entry 8; translation reused.
uncertain: 'Tenku Chushin Ken: Head-Hunting' is my translation of the technique name (no English source).
'Fellow disciple' for the kana 'brother disciple'.

22.en: A Cronos tribe warrior and martial artist living on planet Cronos. The son of Kirai, the Taoist master who founded Tenku Chushin Ken, he has attained full mastery of both Tenku Chushin Ken and Tenku Shin Ken. Rom likes to use "Tenku Chushin Ken: Whirlwind Kick." The purpose of Tenku Chushin Ken is to defeat evil and protect justice and truth, and in fact Rom's family are aliens who came to planet Cronos to build up their strength. He values justice above all and has a strong heart that never forgives evil, but he seems to be bad with women. Also, although he is polite and strict with himself, he seems to be a little soft on his younger sister Leina. By drawing out the power of Kenro, the sword inherited from his father, he can merge into the giant robots Kenryuu and Baikanfu. With his many Tenku Chushin Ken techniques and a distinctive catchphrase that he delivers suddenly, from out of nowhere, he plunges villains into the depths of terror, and after defeating Gyandlar, he sets off across dimensions (reincarnates) to save a universe ruled by darkness. Incidentally, in the original story Kenryuu and Baikanfu are petrified and left behind on planet Cronos at that time.
uncertain: 'Taoist master' for [jp].
'Whirlwind Kick' is my translation of the technique name.

135.en: Kaine's mother. She is divorced from her husband, Jim Austin, who was an Alliance soldier. She worked at the immigration control center of the colony Alucard, but went missing during the fighting with Giganos. A woman faithful to her duties and valuing ethics, she is someone Kaine respects, though he does not say so out loud.

136.name_jp: ウェルナー・フリッツ
136.en: A member of the Practice Squad, the elite unit under Meio. He is 19 years old and holds the rank of warrant officer. Even among the three, his eyes are especially nasty. The Practice Squad's loyalty to Meio is strong, reaching the level of worship.
uncertain: 'Practice Squad' follows English Wikipedia; the kana is Practices ([jp]).
Gender: male, from the 'boys' unit' wording elsewhere and the group description.

137.en: A member of the Practice Squad, the elite unit under Meio. He is 19 years old and holds the rank of warrant officer. When first introduced, the Practice Squad was an obnoxious elite group, but as the story progressed, their devoted actions toward Meio won support, and they gained fans.

138.en: One of Gon Jem's Four Heavenly Kings, who pilots the Stark Gan-Dolla. His rank is captain. Fittingly for the Gon Jem Squad, which is called "Giganos's filth," he has an extremely cruel personality, and is described as a murderer wearing a military uniform. He has a big scar on his face and always has a 5-sun (about 15 cm) nail in his mouth. Maybe he is short on iron.
uncertain: '5-sun nail' kept with the metric gloss.
'Giganos's filth' ([jp]) vs. English Wikipedia 'Garbage of Giganos'.

145.en: The founder and supreme ruler of the United Empire Giganos. It seems he was originally a high-ranking officer of some country. He starts the invasion of Earth to eliminate everyone and every idea belonging to the Earth Alliance as inferior and create a new order in space. He loves Earth so much that, in order to wipe out the Alliance forces without harming Earth's beauty, he even carries out pinpoint attacks using mass drivers. He holds an elitist ideology of thoroughgoing ability supremacy, and keeps as pets rumble fish, which kill each other if several are put in the same tank.
uncertain: 'Rumble fish' translated from the kana ([jp]).

146.en: The commander of the Asia theater secret guard unit of Giganos. His rank is colonel. He has four skilled subordinates called Gon Jem's Four Heavenly Kings. He is rough and vulgar by nature, and that shows in his way of fighting too: even in Metal Armor combat, he excels at close combat with a huge Azure Dragon sword. Having done a number of dirty jobs, he seems to have connections in the military. He is also surprisingly caring toward his subordinates and is trusted by them. With a sacred straw rope (shimenawa) strung around his neck, he resembles a Tosa fighting dog.
uncertain: 'Gon Jem' (English Wikipedia) vs. kana 'Gun Jem'.
'Shimenawa' kept and glossed.

147.en: A 16-year-old civilian boy who lived on the space colony Alucard and attends the Astronaut Academy. His parents are divorced; his father is a staff officer of the Alliance forces and his mother works at the colony's immigration control center. He gets along well with Tapp and Light. During Giganos's attack on Alucard, the three happened to be on the scene in town where a man carrying a data disk of a secret weapon was shot dead by someone, and were entrusted with the disk by the man as he died, and they ended up becoming pilots of the secret weapon, the Dragonars. However, since the Dragonars had a system that could be piloted only by those who had completed pilot registration, they went along with the Alliance forces as events unfolded. By personality he is more of a flirt, but he is a straightforward type who acts without thinking too much, and the typical bully-boy type, oddly loyal and with a strong sense of justice. As a result he stirs up trouble here and there and drags those around him in. His hairstyle was originally a pompadour, but the demon sergeant cut it, giving him his current look. He falls in love at first sight with Linda, whom he met as a refugee from the Moon.
uncertain: 'Kaine' (Wikipedia/MAL) vs. fan spelling 'Kane'.
'Bully-boy type' translates the idiom 'gaki daisho' (kid ringleader).

149.en: One of Gon Jem's Four Heavenly Kings, who pilots the Stark Gewai. His rank is captain. He is the biggest man in the Gon Jem Squad, with a skeleton that does not seem human, but his wits are weak to match. He has a very violent personality and a habit of firing his machine cannon everywhere when something displeases him, which is extremely annoying. Looking for a wife.

150.name_jp: ジェームス・Ｃ・ダグラス
150.en: A soldier of the Earth Alliance Forces, with the rank of lieutenant. The official pilot of Dragonar-1. Because Kaine stole the Dragonar-1 that he should rightfully have ridden, he reluctantly became the training officer for Kaine and the others, an unfortunate man. Perhaps for that reason, although he is a capable soldier, he got no further than captain even after promotions. He becomes a crying drunk when he gets drunk.
uncertain: Gender from the game text ('kare') and ja Wikipedia.
'Training officer' for [jp].

151.en: One of Gon Jem's Four Heavenly Kings, who pilots the Stark Dauzehn. His rank is lieutenant. He has looks that could be called handsome, but among the four he is the most calculating, cold-blooded and vindictive. His manner of death was, truly, too awful. I cannot forget the sight of him threatening Linda while licking a knife.
uncertain: The last sentence is the writer's own first-person comment in the Japanese ('forgettable') and is kept as such.

152.en: One of the refugees aboard the transport ship Idaho, a mysterious beautiful teacher. In truth, however, she is a second lieutenant of Earth Alliance Forces intelligence, in charge of monitoring the D-Weapons and guarding Linda. At 22, she is the most adult of the three heroines. She is a big-sister figure to Linda and Rose, and is calm and composed. Perhaps for that reason she gets along with Light, but it did not progress much. A mature woman full of kindness and consideration for others, she has the flaw of being a bad drunk.
uncertain: 'Second lieutenant' for [jp] (English Wikipedia says only 'Lt').

153.en: A 16-year-old student at the same Astronaut Academy as Kaine, from New York. He becomes the pilot of Dragonar-2. He is the so-called "gentle and strong" type, but like Kaine and the others, a cheerful boy with a light attitude.
